1.0.s:
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ
lāṭyāyanīye śrautasūtre prathamaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ
1.0.d:
श्रीगणेशाय नमः
लाट्यायनीये श्रौतसूत्रे प्रथमः प्रपाठकः

1.1.m: Now, when a ritual rule has no specific attribution, it is a general governing rule for all sacrificial rites.
And the rule for mantras [is indicated] by mentioning the beginning [words].
The beginning of the subsequent [mantra] marks the end of the previous one.
Because of the rule of monotone recitation, and where there is no specific instruction, only the udgātṛ priest should perform the mantras and the ritual actions.
The mantras whose ends are not designated [extend] as far as the yajus [formula].
An officiating priest must be of distinguished descent, learned in the Veda, of upright conduct, eloquent, lacking neither too few nor too many limbs, of middle age, neither too dark nor too pale.
And the patron of the sacrifice is explained by the first three qualities.
If he intends not to act [as priest], he should refuse the soma herald after saying: "Homage to King Soma!"
If he intends to act, he should respond with the formula: "Proclaim to me what is great!"
Knowing, "I shall act," he should not abandon that [purpose], even if not invited.
The dwelling [host] should have salted food brought to the soma herald with curd.
He should send forth the prastotṛ priest and the subrahmaṇya priest in advance of the ritual actions.
The sacrificial ground should slope to the east or north, be grassy, treeless, and level.
And there should be waters in front of it.
In the absence of that, a great tree, a well, or a highway [should be in front].
And there should be no higher ground nearby.
And in front, it should be the size of a sacrificial ground.
In malevolent rites, the reverse [applies], except for the higher ground and the size of the sacrificial ground.
He should go himself at the purchase [of soma] or on the day of preparation.

1.1.s: udaṅṅeva tu gṛhebhyaḥ prathamaṃ devo devametviti
1.1.d: उदङ्ङेव तु गृहेभ्यः प्रथमं देवो देवमेत्विति
1.1.m: First indeed toward the north from the houses, with: "May the god go to the god!"
Having gone far, with: "Leaving behind evil deeds!"
Having entered the path, with: "You are the vehicle of the birds!"
Stepping onto the northern edge of the altar and looking south, with: "Fathers, you have become...!"
Dhānañjayya holds that he should insert the yajus formula while offering [food].

1.2.m: He should drink the honey-mixture offering separately with the quarters of the Sāvitrī verse.
In that rite, they bring this: the straw seat, the foot-washing water, the guest-water, the water for sipping, and the honey-mixture offering.

1.2.s: idadannamayaṃ rasa imā gāvaḥ sahaśriyeti tu purastādekaikasya
1.2.d: इददन्नमयं रस इमा गावः सहश्रियेति तु पुरस्तादेकैकस्य
1.2.m: Before each [draught], however, [he recites]: "This is food, this is essence, these are cows along with prosperity!"

1.2.s: vāgvahu bahu me bhūyāditi prathamasyopariṣṭāt prāṇo vai vāco bhūyān bahurme bhūyo bhūyāditi dvitīyasya mano vāva sarvaṃ sarvaṃ mebhūyāditi tṛtīyasya
1.2.d: वाग्वहु बहु मे भूयादिति प्रथमस्योपरिष्टात् प्राणो वै वाचो भूयान् बहुर्मे भूयो भूयादिति द्वितीयस्य मनो वाव सर्वं सर्वं मेभूयादिति तृतीयस्य
1.2.m: After the first [draught]: "May speech, abundant, be abundant for me!"; after the second: "Breath is indeed greater than speech; may it be increasingly abundant for me!"; after the third: "Mind is indeed everything; may everything be mine!"
[All these formulas] end with the exclamation svāhā.

1.2.s: rasosi vānaspatyo rasaṃ mayi dhehīti madhumanthasya pibediti gautamo vānaspatya iti pravacanaṃ
1.2.d: रसोसि वानस्पत्यो रसं मयि धेहीति मधुमन्थस्य पिबेदिति गौतमो वानस्पत्य इति प्रवचनं
1.2.m: With: "You are the arboreal essence; place essence in me," he should drink the honey mash—so says Gautama; "arboreal" is the canonical reading.

1.2.s: tathā dadhimanthodamanthayoḥ payasyo'payasya iti tu rasādeśaḥ
1.2.d: तथा दधिमन्थोदमन्थयोः पयस्योऽपयस्य इति तु रसादेशः
1.2.m: Likewise in the curd mash and water mash, the specification of the essence is "milky" and "watery" respectively.

1.2.s: etenaiva pravacane kālindaḥ sārasvata iti vā
1.2.d: एतेनैव प्रवचने कालिन्दः सारस्वत इति वा
1.2.m: In that same canonical reading, [the water mash may be called] "descended from the Yamunā" or "descended from the Sarasvatī".
He should give the remainder to a brāhmaṇa.
In the absence of such, having sprinkled it with water, [he may give it] to a non-brāhmaṇa.
When the cow is announced, he should say: "Do it!"
Or: "Release the cow; let the cow eat grass!"
For all those undertaking the ritual action, the wearing of the sacred thread and the sipping of water are obligatory.
There must be no intervention and no turning away from the constituent parts of the sacrifice.
And where there is no specific instruction, the action is performed facing east.

1.2.s: krīte rājani subrahmaṇya uttareṇa somavahanaṃ gatvāntareṇeṣe śamīśākhāṃ palāśaśākhāṃ vā sapalāśāṃ pāṇau kṛtvā'vatiṣṭheta
1.2.d: क्रीते राजनि सुब्रह्मण्य उत्तरेण सोमवहनं गत्वान्तरेणेषे शमीशाखां पलाशशाखां वा सपलाशां पाणौ कृत्वाऽवतिष्ठेत
1.2.m: When the King [Soma] has been purchased, the subrahmaṇya priest, having gone north of the soma-cart, should stand between the two shafts holding a leafy branch of śamī or of palāśa in his hand.
In the subrahmaṇyā litany, he should await the adhvaryu priest's direction everywhere.
Holding the reins, he should urge the two draft oxen with the branch, the right one first.
As it moves eastward, he should summon three times: "Subrahmaṇyom!"

1.2.s: pūrvveṇa patnīśālāṃ vimukte chadiṣi śākhāmavaguhya tāmevaiṣāmanūtkramya yathārthaṃ syāt
1.2.d: पूर्व्वेण पत्नीशालां विमुक्ते छदिषि शाखामवगुह्य तामेवैषामनूत्क्रम्य यथार्थं स्यात्
1.2.m: East of the wife's hall, when the cart-covering is unfastened, having concealed the branch, having stepped out alongside that same shaft, he should go as needed.
He should give the right draft ox to the subrahmaṇya priest.
"Both [oxen]," states the Śāṭyāyana tradition, because of their connection with the ritual action.

1.3.s: ātithyāyā ssthitāyāṃ dakṣiṇasya dvāravāhoḥ parastāttiṣṭhannantarvedideśe'nvārabdhe yajamāne patnyāñca subrahmaṇyomiti triruktvā nigadaṃ brūyādindrāgaccha hariva āgaccha medhātithermeṣavṛṣaṇaśvasya mene gaurāvaskandinnahalyāyai jārakauśikabrāhmaṇagautamabruvāṇaitāvadahe sutyāmiti yāvadahe syāt
1.3.d: आतिथ्याया स्स्थितायां दक्षिणस्य द्वारवाहोः परस्तात्तिष्ठन्नन्तर्वेदिदेशेऽन्वारब्धे यजमाने पत्न्याञ्च सुब्रह्मण्योमिति त्रिरुक्त्वा निगदं ब्रूयादिन्द्रागच्छ हरिव आगच्छ मेधातिथेर्मेषवृषणश्वस्य मेने गौरावस्कन्दिन्नहल्यायै जारकौशिकब्राह्मणगौतमब्रुवाणैतावदहे सुत्यामिति यावदहे स्यात्
1.3.m: When the hospitality rite is completed, standing beyond the right door-post in the area within the altar, while the patron of the sacrifice and his wife are holding on [to him], having uttered "Subrahmaṇyom" three times, he should recite the ritual formula: "Come, Indra! Come, possessor of bay steeds! Ram of Medhātithi! Vṛṣaṇaśva's woman! Gour-leaper! Lover of Ahalyā! Son of Kuśika! Brāhmaṇa! Calling yourself Gautama! At the soma-pressing day on such-and-such a day!"—[naming] on whichever day it is to be.
"O gods! O brāhmaṇas! Come! Come! Come!"—so says Gautama.
"Come!" comes before the invocation of the gods, holds Dhānañjayya.
He should pause at the first two praṇavas;
The patron of the sacrifice and his wife, desiring the ritual invitation, [say:] ‘O subrahmaṇya priest, invite us!’
Thus at the end of all the upasads;
Before the declaration of the soma-pressing day, there is the reciting of names.

1.3.s: agnīṣomīyavapāyāhutāyām parihṛtāsu vasatīvarīṣu prātaranuvākopakramavelāyāmasau yajata iti pratyekaṃ gṛhṇīyādyajamānanāmadheyānyamuṣya putraḥ pautro napteti pūrveṣāṃ
1.3.d: अग्नीषोमीयवपायाहुतायाम् परिहृतासु वसतीवरीषु प्रातरनुवाकोपक्रमवेलायामसौ यजत इति प्रत्येकं गृह्णीयाद्यजमाननामधेयान्यमुष्य पुत्रः पौत्रो नप्तेति पूर्वेषां
1.3.m: When the omentum of the Agnīṣomīya [victim] has been offered, when the vasatīvarī waters have been carried around, [and] at the time of beginning the morning recitation, he should name each of the names of the patron of the sacrifice, saying ‘So-and-so sacrifices’, [and] ‘the son, grandson, [or] great-grandson of So-and-so’ with respect to his ancestors;
then with respect to the descendants, according to seniority, of the women and men who may be living;
having said ‘and of those to be born’, he should conclude beginning with the declaration of the soma-pressing day.
The [recitation] that was omitted at the omentum of the Agnīṣomīya [victim] occurs in the sādyaḥkra rites.

1.4.m: In the Agniṣṭut rites, the recited ritual formula is addressed to Agni.

1.4.s: tatra gautamīyamagna āgaccha rohitābhyāṃ vṛhadbhāno dhūmaketo jātavedo vicarṣaṇa āṅgirasa brāhmaṇāṅgirasa bruvāṇeti prāk sutyādeśāt
1.4.d: तत्र गौतमीयमग्न आगच्छ रोहिताभ्यां वृहद्भानो धूमकेतो जातवेदो विचर्षण आङ्गिरस ब्राह्मणाङ्गिरस ब्रुवाणेति प्राक् सुत्यादेशात्
1.4.m: There Gautama's [form is]: ‘Agni, come with your two bay steeds, of vast brilliance, of smoky banner, knower of creatures, all-seeing, descendant of Aṅgiras, brāhmaṇa, being called a descendant of Aṅgiras’—prior to the declaration of the soma-pressing day.

1.4.s: atha dhānañjayyo'gna āgaccha rohitava āgaccha bharadvājasyājasahasaḥ sūno vārāvaskandinnuṣaso jāretyāṅgirasaprabhṛtisamānam
1.4.d: अथ धानञ्जय्योऽग्न आगच्छ रोहितव आगच्छ भरद्वाजस्याजसहसः सूनो वारावस्कन्दिन्नुषसो जारेत्याङ्गिरसप्रभृतिसमानम्
1.4.m: Then Dhānañjayya [holds that it is]: ‘Agni, come with your two bay steeds; come, child of Bharadvāja's vigorous power, son of strength, assailer of enclosures, lover of the dawn’—the rest from ‘descendant of Aṅgiras’ being the same.
In the unexpressed [subrahmaṇyā litanies], he should say: ‘Indra, mighty one!’ [and] ‘all [gods]!’
And in the case of the two unexpressed morning pressings.
Between the abhiṣecanīya and daśapeya rites, there is always the reciting of names.
In multi-day periods, he should call at the beginning and end of each day.
Beginning from the Agnīṣomīya [day] in ahīna sacrifices, all [calls] include the reciting of names.
In sacrificial sessions, the reciting of names of the consecrated occurs in the order of their consecration.
After the atirātra, there is no reciting of names.
At its end [the formula is]: ‘Tomorrow is the soma-pressing day,’ according to Gautama.
‘Today is the soma-pressing day,’ according to Śāṇḍilya.
Dhānañjayya [holds that] there is no calling; and there is reciting of names in the final three [calls].
‘In the final two,’ says Gautama.
That being so, at the omentum of the Agnīṣomīya [victim], there is no reciting of names according to Dhānañjayya, or no calling at all.
According to Śāṇḍilya, there is no reciting of names in sacrificial sessions anywhere.
After the atirātra, there is one Āgneyī [call] in the second fifteen-day period;
In the third, all [calls] prior to the Trikadruka days [are Āgneyī].
In the Kauṇḍapāyina and Tāpaścita sacrifices, knowing that the soma-pressing day is on the twelfth day, Dhānañjayya holds that the calling indicates the measured period.
The other [calls have]: ‘Come to the soma-pressing day!’

1.4.s: ūrddhvaṃ cātirātrāt prathamasya sārasvatasya prāk śvaḥ sutyāyāḥ
1.4.d: ऊर्द्ध्वं चातिरात्रात् प्रथमस्य सारस्वतस्य प्राक् श्वः सुत्यायाः
1.4.m: And after the atirātra of the first Sārasvata [session], up to the call ‘Tomorrow is the soma-pressing day’.
In the Kauṇḍapāyina and Sārasvata sacrifices, in the iṣṭi courses, it is as on a soma-pressing day, according to Śāṇḍilya.
Likewise during the agnihotra month; likewise during the agnihotra month.

1.5.s: sarvatrānādeśe parisāmāni prastotā gāyet svādhyāyavat svāsu
1.5.d: सर्वत्रानादेशे परिसामानि प्रस्तोता गायेत् स्वाध्यायवत् स्वासु
1.5.m: Everywhere where not specified, the prastotṛ priest should sing the parisāmans as in personal Vedic recitation on their own [verses].
Those that correspond to triplets on triplets; the others three times.
Between the cātvāla pit and the utkara rubbish-heap is the path of movement everywhere when not specified.

1.5.s: agnau cīyamāne paścimena pucchaṅgatvā dakṣiṇe'pikakṣe tiṣṭhedyatra vopadadhyuḥ
1.5.d: अग्नौ चीयमाने पश्चिमेन पुच्छङ्गत्वा दक्षिणेऽपिकक्षे तिष्ठेद्यत्र वोपदध्युः
1.5.m: While the fire altar is being piled, having gone along the west of the tail, he should stand at the southern wing-joint, or wherever they are laying [the bricks].
The two wing-joints are to the west of the wings.

1.5.s: puṣkarapalāśa upadhīyamāne hiraṇmaye puruṣe svayamātṛṇāsu ca śarkarāsu vyāhṛtisāmāni gāyed yajamānsatyaṃ puruṣo bhūrbhuvaḥ svarityetāsu pṛthak
1.5.d: पुष्करपलाश उपधीयमाने हिरण्मये पुरुषे स्वयमातृणासु च शर्करासु व्याहृतिसामानि गायेद् यजमान्सत्यं पुरुषो भूर्भुवः स्वरित्येतासु पृथक्
1.5.m: When the lotus-leaf, the golden man, and the naturally perforated stones and pebbles are being laid, he should sing the Vyāhṛti sāmans—the patron of the sacrifice [sings] separately on these: ‘Satyam’, ‘Puruṣaḥ’, and ‘Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ’.

1.5.s: teṣā sthāne svayaṃ cinvāna ṛtanidhanamājyadohaṃ puruṣavratamekānugānaṃ rathantaraṃ vāmadevyaṃ bṛhaditi
1.5.d: तेषा स्थाने स्वयं चिन्वान ऋतनिधनमाज्यदोहं पुरुषव्रतमेकानुगानं रथन्तरं वामदेव्यं बृहदिति
1.5.m: In their place, when he himself is piling [the altar]: the Ṛtanidhana, the Ājyadoha, the Puruṣavrata with a single singing-along, the Rathantara, the Vāmadevya, and the Bṛhat.
Those beginning with the Rathantara alternate with repeated Lokasāmans.

1.5.s: sañcitamagniṃ dakṣiṇena gatvāgna āyūṣīti pratyaṅmukhastiṣṭhaṃśchirasi gāyatraṃ gāyenniruktam
1.5.d: सञ्चितमग्निं दक्षिणेन गत्वाग्न आयूषीति प्रत्यङ्मुखस्तिष्ठंश्छिरसि गायत्रं गायेन्निरुक्तम्
1.5.m: Having gone along the south of the piled fire altar, standing facing west, he should sing the gāyatra chant distinctly on its head with [the verse] ‘agna āyūṃṣi’.

1.5.s: pratyābrajya rathantaraṃ dakṣiṇe pakṣa udaṅmukhaḥ paścādvā prāṅmukhaḥ
1.5.d: प्रत्याब्रज्य रथन्तरं दक्षिणे पक्ष उदङ्मुखः पश्चाद्वा प्राङ्मुखः
1.5.m: Having returned, [he sings] the Rathantara at the southern wing facing north, or from behind facing east.

1.5.s: paścimena pucche gatvā bṛhaduttare pakṣe dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ paścādvā prāṅmukhaḥ
1.5.d: पश्चिमेन पुच्छे गत्वा बृहदुत्तरे पक्षे दक्षिणामुखः पश्चाद्वा प्राङ्मुखः

1.5.s: pratyābrajya yajñāyajñīyaṃ pucche saṃvatsaraśceddaikṣaḥ sautyo vā
1.5.d: प्रत्याब्रज्य यज्ञायज्ञीयं पुच्छे संवत्सरश्चेद्दैक्षः सौत्यो वा
1.5.m: Having returned, [he sings] the yajñāyajñīya melody at the tail, if the year is during the consecration or during the soma-pressing.
Standing at the right armpit, he should sing the vāmadevya melody; at the left [armpit], the prajāpatihṛdaya.
Gautama holds that these are sung having gone along the north of the fire.

1.5.s: etānyeva pradakṣiṇaṃ pratyantāddhānañjayyo yajñāyajñīyaṃ pucche prajāpatihṛdayasthāne ca vāmadevyam
1.5.d: एतान्येव प्रदक्षिणं प्रत्यन्ताद्धानञ्जय्यो यज्ञायज्ञीयं पुच्छे प्रजापतिहृदयस्थाने च वामदेव्यम्
1.5.m: Dhānañjayya holds that having gone circumambulating clockwise from the western border, these same [sāmans are sung]: the yajñāyajñīya at the tail, and the vāmadevya at the place of the prajāpatihṛdaya.

1.5.s: dakṣiṇenāgniṃ gatvā gautamīye vyatyayaṃ ye pakṣayoḥ śāṇḍilyaḥ
1.5.d: दक्षिणेनाग्निं गत्वा गौतमीये व्यत्ययं ये पक्षयोः शाण्डिल्यः
1.5.m: Śāṇḍilya holds that having gone along the south of the fire, in Gautama's view there is an inversion of those on the two wings.
And having sung at the head, [then] on the northern wing,
And at the northern flank, touching his own heart, he sings the prajāpatihṛdaya; along the path of the adhvaryu priest, the śyaita.

1.6.s: pravargyavatyuttareṇa samrāḍāsandīṃ gatvā paścāttiṣṭhannadhvaryupreṣitastyagnāyiriti gāyat padāya padāya stobhet
1.6.d: प्रवर्ग्यवत्युत्तरेण सम्राडासन्दीं गत्वा पश्चात्तिष्ठन्नध्वर्युप्रेषितस्त्यग्नायिरिति गायत् पदाय पदाय स्तोभेत्
1.6.m: At a rite possessing a pravargya, having gone north of the emperor's stool and standing behind it, urged by the adhvaryu priest, he should sing the agnāyi verse, making a stobha interjection for each quarter-verse.
He should utter the stobha-speech only at the cadence.

1.6.s: upagrahaprabhṛtīni svarayanta upeyurye gharma upayuktāḥ syuḥ
1.6.d: उपग्रहप्रभृतीनि स्वरयन्त उपेयुर्ये घर्म उपयुक्ताः स्युः
1.6.m: Those who are employed in the gharma rite should join in singing the tone, beginning from the upagraha pause.
And having reached the spot of the āhavanīya fire,
while water is being sprinkled around, having touched water, [he sings] the vārṣāhara melody.
When it has been sprinkled around, [he sings] the iṣṭāhotrīya melody.
All should join in its cadence.
If they carry the gharma vessels across water, he should not wait for the sprinkling.
Returning, [he sings] the śyaita melody, either on a triplet or on a single verse.
The patron of the sacrifice should join in after the cadence.

1.6.s: pūrvayā dvārā prapadyottareṇāgnīngatvā paścādgārhapatyasya tiṣṭhan mahāvīrāyatanaṃ prekṣamāṇo vāmadevyaṃ gāyediti dhānañjayyaḥ
1.6.d: पूर्वया द्वारा प्रपद्योत्तरेणाग्नीन्गत्वा पश्चाद्गार्हपत्यस्य तिष्ठन् महावीरायतनं प्रेक्षमाणो वामदेव्यं गायेदिति धानञ्जय्यः
1.6.m: Having entered through the eastern door and gone along the north of the fires, standing behind the gārhapatya fire and gazing at the spot of the mahāvīra vessel, he should sing the vāmadevya melody—thus Dhānañjayya.
Śāṇḍilya says that they end with the śyaita.
Some say they are to be performed on account of appropriateness.
Or one should perform them at one's own sacrifice, say some.
At the dīkṣaṇīyā offering he should sing the two tārkṣya sāmans on the verses beginning with 'tyam ū ṣu'.
At the prāyaṇīyā offering, [he sings] the bhārgava melody containing the word 'pra'.
At the ātithyā offering, the gāyatrī sāman and the auśana.
When they anoint the gharma cauldron, there [he sings] the śārṅga melody.
When they place the silver and gold pieces, then [he sings] the śukra and candra melodies.
When he kindles [the fire], then [he sings] the two tanū melodies of the gharma.
When they announce that it has glowed, then [he sings] the rocana of the gharma, or [the rocana] of Indra.
When they bring near the two milch-cows, then [he sings] the dhenu melody.

1.6.s: tasya devatāyai sopāyaṃ stobhamāharenna pādāyeti gautamaḥ
1.6.d: तस्य देवतायै सोपायं स्तोभमाहरेन्न पादायेति गौतमः
1.6.m: For its deity he should insert the stobha interjection with its approach, not for the quarter-verse—thus Gautama.
He should repeat the final quarter-verse, as in the vāmadevya melody with five cadences.
When they bring the milk, then [he sings] the payas melody.
When they pour it in, then [he sings] the sindhu sāman on 'ā tvā viśantu'.
When they grasp it with the tongs, then [he sings] the two śapha melodies of Vasiṣṭha.
While it is being carried, [he sings] the two pakṣa melodies of the vrata.
When it has been offered, [he sings] the two vrata melodies of the Aśvins, or those of Day and Night.
When they proceed with the two rauhiṇa sacrificial cakes, then [he sings] the rājana and rauhiṇaka melodies.

1.6.s: parigharm samrāḍāsandyā samāropayanti tadārūḍhavadāṅgirasamita eta iti svarṇidhanaṃ
1.6.d: परिघर्म् सम्राडासन्द्या समारोपयन्ति तदारूढवदाङ्गिरसमित एत इति स्वर्णिधनं
1.6.m: When they mount the parigharma cauldron onto the emperor's stool, then [he sings] the āṅgirasa containing the word 'ārūḍha', beginning with 'ita etaḥ', having 'svar' as its cadence.

1.6.s: ṛṅmayo yajurmayaḥ sāmamayo gharmo bhavatīti hyāha
1.6.d: ऋङ्मयो यजुर्मयः साममयो घर्मो भवतीति ह्याह
1.6.m: For indeed it is said: 'The gharma cauldron becomes composed of ṛc, composed of yajus, and composed of sāman.'
When they lead forward the fire, there [he sings] the vrata of Agni.
[When they lead forward] Agni and Soma, there [he sings] the two vrata melodies of both.
On the soma-pressing day, day after day, [he sings] the yajñasārathya melody.
If the anūbandhyā offering is an ox, [he sings] the aukṣṇa melody at the cleft.
At the curds offering, [he sings] the svara melody with 'payas' as its cadence.
Having begun, he should carry them through to completion until the conclusion of the sacrifice.

1.7.m: Intending to erect the post of udumbara wood, he should go by the east of the sacrificial ground if his dwelling is to the south.

1.7.s: pūrvau sadaso dvāryau śvabhrāvantareṇa prapadyāgneṇaudumbarīṃ gatvodaṅmukhastiṣṭhannadhvaryuṇā sahocchrayet dyutānastveti
1.7.d: पूर्वौ सदसो द्वार्यौ श्वभ्रावन्तरेण प्रपद्याग्नेणौदुम्बरीं गत्वोदङ्मुखस्तिष्ठन्नध्वर्युणा सहोच्छ्रयेत् द्युतानस्त्वेति
1.7.m: Entering between the two eastern door-posts and the pits of the sadas, and going along the front of the audumbarī post, standing facing north, he should erect it together with the adhvaryu priest with [the formula]: 'May Dyutāna...'
He should place it down into the pit with [the words]: '...of Ayu.'

1.7.s: avadhāya japennamaḥ samudrāya namaḥ samudrasya cakṣase | mā mā yūnarvā hāsīdūrgasyūrjjodā ūrjjamme dehyūrjaṃ me dehyannaṃ me dehyannaṃ me dhehīti
1.7.d: अवधाय जपेन्नमः समुद्राय नमः समुद्रस्य चक्षसे । मा मा यूनर्वा हासीदूर्गस्यूर्ज्जोदा ऊर्ज्जम्मे देह्यूर्जं मे देह्यन्नं मे देह्यन्नं मे धेहीति
1.7.m: Having placed it down, he should whisper: 'Homage to the ocean, homage to the eye of the ocean! May the courser not abandon me in my youth; you are vigor, giver of vigor, give me vigor, give me vigor, give me food, bestow on me food!'
They should not let go of it until it is thatched.

1.7.s: adhvaryyuṇābhihutāyāṃ juhuyāt tasyaivāvṛtāntareṇa viśākhe ghṛtena dyāvāpṛthivī āprīṇāthāsvāheti pūrvāṃ
1.7.d: अध्वर्य्युणाभिहुतायां जुहुयात् तस्यैवावृतान्तरेण विशाखे घृतेन द्यावापृथिवी आप्रीणाथास्वाहेति पूर्वां
1.7.m: When an oblation has been poured upon it by the adhvaryu priest, he should make an offering in the same manner as the adhvaryu priest: the first [offering] between the two branches with [the formula]: 'With ghee, O Heaven and Earth, be pleased, svāhā!'
The second with [the formula]: 'To Prajāpati, svāhā!'

1.7.s: anyatarāṃ vā svāhākāradvitīyāṃ yathā bhūmimājyaṃ prāpsyatīti
1.7.d: अन्यतरां वा स्वाहाकारद्वितीयां यथा भूमिमाज्यं प्राप्स्यतीति
1.7.m: Or [he may make] either of the two with a second svāhā-call, so that the clarified butter reaches the ground.

1.7.s: adhastādviśākhasya parigṛhya japeddivi devāṃ dṛha mayi prajāmiti
1.7.d: अधस्ताद्विशाखस्य परिगृह्य जपेद्दिवि देवां दृह मयि प्रजामिति
1.7.m: Grasping it below the fork, he should whisper: 'Establish the gods in heaven, off-spring in me!'

1.7.s: antarīkṣe vayāsi dṛha mayi paśūniti madhye
1.7.d: अन्तरीक्षे वयासि दृह मयि पशूनिति मध्ये
1.7.m: In the middle: 'Establish birds in the intermediate space, cattle in me!'
At the base: 'Establish plants in the middle of the earth, kinsmen in me!'
After the offering, [the duties belong to] the patron of the sacrifice, says Dhānañjayya.
He should do them himself, say Gautama and Śāṇḍilya.

1.7.s: avacchādyamānāyāṃ divyaṃ chadmasi santatināma viśvajanasya chāyā namaste'stu māmā hiṃ sīriti
1.7.d: अवच्छाद्यमानायां दिव्यं छद्मसि सन्ततिनाम विश्वजनस्य छाया नमस्तेऽस्तु मामा हिं सीरिति
1.7.m: While it is being thatched, [he whispers]: 'You are a heavenly cover, Santati by name, shade of all people; homage be to you; do not harm me!'

1.7.s: dakṣiṇena śvabhrān gatvā parau dvāryāvantareṇa prapadyaitat kuryyāditi śāṇḍilyaḥ
1.7.d: दक्षिणेन श्वभ्रान् गत्वा परौ द्वार्यावन्तरेण प्रपद्यैतत् कुर्य्यादिति शाण्डिल्यः
1.7.m: Having gone south of the pits and entering between the other two door-posts, he should perform this, says Śāṇḍilya.

1.8.m: They should address the sacrificial post as it is being erected with [the formula]: 'O friend of men, upright-bearing...'
These very [formulas] are the places for modification according to how many [posts] there may be.
Wherever they, while standing, can see it being erected, says Śāṇḍilya.

1.8.s: antarvedyeveti dhānañjayyo na bahirvedi yajuravakalpata iti
1.8.d: अन्तर्वेद्येवेति धानञ्जय्यो न बहिर्वेदि यजुरवकल्पत इति
1.8.m: Only inside the altar ground, says Dhānañjayya, for a sacrificial formula is not appropriate outside the altar ground.
When requested by the patron of the sacrifice to sing the Viśvarūpā verses, he should refuse.

1.8.s: gāyeti cedeva brūyānna māmanāmantrya prātaranuvākamupākuryā ityadhvaryyuṃ brūyāt
1.8.d: गायेति चेदेव ब्रूयान्न मामनामन्त्र्य प्रातरनुवाकमुपाकुर्या इत्यध्वर्य्युं ब्रूयात्
1.8.m: If the patron should nevertheless say, 'Sing!', he should say to the adhvaryu priest: 'Do not initiate the morning recitation without summoning me.'

1.8.s: hotāraṃ prātaranuvākāyopaviṣṭaṃ pūrveṇa gatvā yajamānaśca pūrvayā dvārā prapadyāntareṇa havirddhāne pūrveṇa cakre udaṅmukha upaviśet tūṣṇīm
1.8.d: होतारं प्रातरनुवाकायोपविष्टं पूर्वेण गत्वा यजमानश्च पूर्वया द्वारा प्रपद्यान्तरेण हविर्द्धाने पूर्वेण चक्रे उदङ्मुख उपविशेत् तूष्णीम्
1.8.m: Having walked east of the hotṛ priest who is seated for the morning recitation, and having entered together with the patron of the sacrifice through the eastern door, he should sit down silently facing north between the two cart-shed carts, east of the axle.
In front [of him sits] the patron of the sacrifice facing west.

1.8.s: yuñje vācaṃ śatapadīṅgāyet sahasravarttani gāyatraṃ traiṣṭubhaṃ jagadviśvā rūpāṇi sambhṛtā devā okāṃsi cakrira ityetasyāṃ paṅktau trirgāyatraṃ gāyediti dhānañjayyaḥ svādhyāyasvareṇa manasaiva yajamāna upasvaret
1.8.d: युञ्जे वाचं शतपदीङ्गायेत् सहस्रवर्त्तनि गायत्रं त्रैष्टुभं जगद्विश्वा रूपाणि सम्भृता देवा ओकांसि चक्रिर इत्येतस्यां पङ्क्तौ त्रिर्गायत्रं गायेदिति धानञ्जय्यः स्वाध्यायस्वरेण मनसैव यजमान उपस्वरेत्
1.8.m: He should sing the gāyatra melody three times to this paṅkti verse: 'I harness speech, hundred-footed, thousand-pathed, gāyatra, traiṣṭubha, jāgata; all forms collected, the gods have made their abodes', says Dhānañjayya; the patron of the sacrifice should mentally accompany with the pitch of private study.

1.8.s: triṣu triṣu padeṣu gāyediti gautamaḥ pūrvaṃ pūrvamatisṛjan
1.8.d: त्रिषु त्रिषु पदेषु गायेदिति गौतमः पूर्वं पूर्वमतिसृजन्
1.8.m: He should sing upon groups of three quarter-verses, says Gautama, letting go of each preceding one.
If he should sing the Viśvarūpā verses, he should also sing the Jyotis verses.

1.8.s: parihite prātaranuvāke 'ponaptrīyaṃ nāma sūktaṃ purā tasmāddhotāramāramayitvāgrayaṇasya vānuhiṅkāraṃ pavitraṃ dhārayannāstāvaṃ vā prāpya stomayogādagnirjyotirjyotiragnirindro jyotirjyotirindraḥ sūryyo jyotirjyotiḥ sūryya ityeteṣu padeṣu tristrirekaikamabhyāsaṃ manasā gāyatraṃ gāyet
1.8.d: परिहिते प्रातरनुवाके ऽपोनप्त्रीयं नाम सूक्तं पुरा तस्माद्धोतारमारमयित्वाग्रयणस्य वानुहिङ्कारं पवित्रं धारयन्नास्तावं वा प्राप्य स्तोमयोगादग्निर्ज्योतिर्ज्योतिरग्निरिन्द्रो ज्योतिर्ज्योतिरिन्द्रः सूर्य्यो ज्योतिर्ज्योतिः सूर्य्य इत्येतेषु पदेषु त्रिस्त्रिरेकैकमभ्यासं मनसा गायत्रं गायेत्
1.8.m: When the morning recitation has been concluded, before the hymn called Aponaptrīya, having caused the hotṛ priest to pause, or holding the strainer along with the hiṅkāra of the āgrayaṇa cup, or having reached the chanting place, he should mentally sing the gāyatra melody thrice upon each of these words before the yoking of the stoma: 'Agni is light, light is Agni; Indra is light, light is Indra; Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya.'
These are [performed] nowhere other than with the Viśvarūpā verses.
And nowhere other than at a Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice with the Viśvarūpā verses, at a Jyotiṣṭoma sacrifice.

1.9.s: yugapatkarmasu sarveṣūdgāturdakṣiṇamanu bāhuṃ prastotā savyaṃ pratiharttā
1.9.d: युगपत्कर्मसु सर्वेषूद्गातुर्दक्षिणमनु बाहुं प्रस्तोता सव्यं प्रतिहर्त्ता
1.9.m: In all simultaneous ritual actions, the prastotṛ priest stands beside the udgātṛ priest's right arm, and the pratihārtṛ priest beside his left.
When the hotṛ priest, having recited the morning recitation, says, 'Dawn has appeared,' they should then step onto the altar ground with: 'Loose with soft [earth]...'
With the sacrificial formula day after day, says Gautama.
Once in the sacrifice, says Śāṇḍilya.
As often as they step onto it, say some.
As the Vasatīvarī waters are being brought in, they should enter the cart-shed after them.
Touching its front piece with: 'The head of Viṣṇu.'
Entering with: 'Food, vigor!'

1.9.s: antareṇeṣe bāhūnavahṛtya pārṣṇoranudyacchanto yunaymīti rājānamabhimṛśeyuryaḥ prātaḥsavanāya
1.9.d: अन्तरेणेषे बाहूनवहृत्य पार्ष्णोरनुद्यच्छन्तो युनय्मीति राजानमभिमृशेयुर्यः प्रातःसवनाय
1.9.m: Bringing down their arms between the two shafts and lifting their heels, they should touch the King [Soma] that is for the morning pressing with: 'I yoke...'
If they cannot reach [the whole of it], by touching a part only.
The prastotṛ priest should creep forward first.

1.9.s: dakṣiṇasya havirddhānasya paścāt savyāvṛta upaviśeyurṛtasya sadana iti
1.9.d: दक्षिणस्य हविर्द्धानस्य पश्चात् सव्यावृत उपविशेयुरृतस्य सदन इति
1.9.m: Behind the southern cart-shed cart, turning to the left, they should sit down with: 'In the seat of truth.'
They should whisper [the formula] everywhere both before and after the verses upon which they are about to chant.
Here, however, [before and after the verses] of the bahiṣpavamāna chant.

1.9.s: abhiṣute rājanyṛtapātramasīti droṇakalaśamālabhya vānaspatya iti proheyuḥ
1.9.d: अभिषुते राजन्यृतपात्रमसीति द्रोणकलशमालभ्य वानस्पत्य इति प्रोहेयुः
1.9.m: When the King [Soma] is pressed, having touched the droṇakalaśa trough with: 'You are the vessel of truth,' they should push it forward with: 'Belonging to the trees.'
The udgātṛ priest should place the fringe-strainer in his right hand.
If they strike against the axle, they should push it forward again.
Between the axle and the prop-pin he should cast the fringe-strainer without striking [either].
If both are connected together, [he casts it] above them.
[The strainer should be cast] higher and higher over the entire chariot-seat,
if it is a chariot, north of the axle-tree of the chariot.

1.10.s: pratyābrajya grāvno yuñjyāt pradakṣiṇamaṣṭamadeśeṣu sthavīyāṃsyabhyantarāṇi kṛtvā
1.10.d: प्रत्याब्रज्य ग्राव्नो युञ्ज्यात् प्रदक्षिणमष्टमदेशेषु स्थवीयांस्यभ्यन्तराणि कृत्वा
1.10.m: Having returned, he should arrange the pressing-stones clockwise in the eighth-directions, making the thicker parts face inward.
The first is the south-eastern one.
Touching them, they should murmur: 'The Maruts…'

1.10.s: ṛtasadana etajjapitvā yuktā stha vahatetyetāvataiveti dhānañjayyaḥ
1.10.d: ऋतसदन एतज्जपित्वा युक्ता स्थ वहतेत्येतावतैवेति धानञ्जय्यः
1.10.m: Dhānañjayya holds that having murmured this in the seat of truth (ṛtasadana), they should murmur only so much: 'You are yoked, draw!'

1.10.s: paścāt dakṣiṇato vā droṇakalaśamadhyūheyuridamahamimamiti yajamānaśabdaṃ sarvatra yathārthaṃ kuryuḥ
1.10.d: पश्चात् दक्षिणतो वा द्रोणकलशमध्यूहेयुरिदमहमिममिति यजमानशब्दं सर्वत्र यथार्थं कुर्युः
1.10.m: They should slide the droṇakalaśa trough over [the stones] from behind or from the south with 'Here I [slide] this one…', substituting everywhere the name of the patron of the sacrifice according to the purpose.
When [the action is] done by another, they should murmur along the two formulas, except in the case of what is prescribed by the Brāhmaṇa.
This is the rule for optional rites, except for the rite against an enemy.
In that [rite against an enemy], however, after reversing [the arrangement], both the yoking and the sliding are done silently.
With 'Here I [cast out] that one…' he should cast out the south-western [stone] from the eighth-direction.
In the rites concerning an enemy and a friend, he should adapt the two formulas with reference to the king.
And he should designate his subjects, and [subject] them to [his] sustenance.

1.10.s: upāṃśusavano nāma grāvā pañcamastamupariṣṭāddroṇakalaśasya kuryāt rāṣṭrajighāṃsuḥ pratīveśāṃ balavatīṃ viśamādiśan
1.10.d: उपांशुसवनो नाम ग्रावा पञ्चमस्तमुपरिष्टाद्द्रोणकलशस्य कुर्यात् राष्ट्रजिघांसुः प्रतीवेशां बलवतीं विशमादिशन्
1.10.m: There is a fifth pressing-stone named upāṃśusavana; if one desires to destroy a realm, one should place it above the droṇakalaśa trough, designating a powerful neighboring population.
Gautama holds that having performed one of these, he should perform the regular rite.
Dhānañjayya holds that he should perform only that [optional rite].
Śāṇḍilya holds that an optional rite [is performed] by going out through the eastern door at the end of the pṛṣṭha lauds.

1.10.s: pavitreṇa droṇakalaś saṃmṛjyādvasavastveti budhnaṃ rudrāstveti madhyamādityāstveti bilam
1.10.d: पवित्रेण द्रोणकलश् संमृज्याद्वसवस्त्वेति बुध्नं रुद्रास्त्वेति मध्यमादित्यास्त्वेति बिलम्
1.10.m: He should wipe the droṇakalaśa trough with the strainer: the bottom with 'May the Vasus [cleanse] thee…', the middle with 'May the Rudras [cleanse] thee…', and the brim with 'May the Ādityas [cleanse] thee…'.
Dhānañjayya holds that he should wipe each of these three times at each pressing session with one [of the formulas].
Śāṇḍilya holds that [he should wipe] with all [formulas] at all [pressing sessions].
Having shaken out the strainer, they should stretch it out with the fringes pointing north and the navel facing downward, with 'Thy strainer…'.

1.10.s: santatāyāṃ dhārāyāmudgātā japet pra śukretyamuṣya rājyāyeti priyrājānamādiśet
1.10.d: सन्ततायां धारायामुद्गाता जपेत् प्र शुक्रेत्यमुष्य राज्यायेति प्रिय्राजानमादिशेत्
1.10.m: While the stream is continuous, the udgātṛ priest should murmur: 'Go forth, clear…'; with 'for the kingdom of such-and-such' he should name a beloved king,

1.10.s: rājño rājyāyeti vā yajamānasyarddhyai rājño rājyāyeti vā
1.10.d: राज्ञो राज्यायेति वा यजमानस्यर्द्ध्यै राज्ञो राज्यायेति वा
1.10.m: or with 'for the kingdom of the king', or with 'for the prosperity of the patron of the sacrifice, for the kingdom of the king',
or with 'for the kingdom of king Soma'.
He should say only 'of Soma', for the brāhmaṇas have King Soma for their king.

1.10.s: āgrayaṇaṃ gṛhṇannadhvaryurhiṃkaroti tadā pravṛṇīrannagniḥ prastotāhaṃ mānuṣo vṛhaspatirudgātāhaṃ mānuṣo vāyuḥ pratiharttāhaṃ mānuṣa iti
1.10.d: आग्रयणं गृह्णन्नध्वर्युर्हिंकरोति तदा प्रवृणीरन्नग्निः प्रस्तोताहं मानुषो वृहस्पतिरुद्गाताहं मानुषो वायुः प्रतिहर्त्ताहं मानुष इति
1.10.m: When the adhvaryu priest utters the hiṅkāra syllable while drawing the āgrayaṇa cup, then they should select [the priests]: 'Agni is the prastotṛ priest, I am the human one; Bṛhaspati is the udgātṛ priest, I am the human one; Vāyu is the pratihārtṛ priest, I am the human one.'
Dhānañjayya holds that they should not select.
Śāṇḍilya holds that they should indeed select.
They should release it when the bahiṣpavamāna chant has been praised.

1.11.s: uttarāddhavirddhānāt dhruvasthālīharantaḥ paścimenodgātṛn hṛtvā tenaiva pratihareyuḥ
1.11.d: उत्तराद्धविर्द्धानात् ध्रुवस्थालीहरन्तः पश्चिमेनोद्गातृन् हृत्वा तेनैव प्रतिहरेयुः
1.11.m: When carrying the dhruva vessel from the northern havirdhāna cart, they should carry it past the udgātṛ priests from the west and carry it back along the same path.
The prastotṛ priest should maintain contact with the adhvaryu priest as he steps forth;
the pratihārtṛ priest with the udgātṛ priest;
Having touched King [Soma], they should not touch the clarified butter without touching water.
Likewise, King [Soma] after [touching] the clarified butter everywhere.

1.11.s: adhvaryuṇā hute pravṛttahomau juhuyurgatyānupūrvyeṇa bekurānāmāsi sūryometi
1.11.d: अध्वर्युणा हुते प्रवृत्तहोमौ जुहुयुर्गत्यानुपूर्व्येण बेकुरानामासि सूर्योमेति
1.11.m: When the offering has been made by the adhvaryu priest, they should offer the two pravṛtta oblations in the order of their arrival with 'Thou art named Bekurā…', 'My sun…'.

1.11.s: ssutasome tvadhikāmudgātā juhuyāt saṃveśāyopaveśāyeti yathāsavanaṃ chandāsyādiśan
1.11.d: स्सुतसोमे त्वधिकामुद्गाता जुहुयात् संवेशायोपवेशायेति यथासवनं छन्दास्यादिशन्
1.11.m: When the soma has been pressed, however, the udgātṛ priest should offer an additional oblation with 'For lying down, for sitting down…', naming the meters according to the pressing session.

1.11.s: ṛcsāmeti svāhākārāntayā tṛtīyāṃ sarvatra sa eveti śāṇḍilyaḥ
1.11.d: ऋच्सामेति स्वाहाकारान्तया तृतीयां सर्वत्र स एवेति शाण्डिल्यः
1.11.m: Śāṇḍilya holds that he alone [offers] everywhere the third [oblation] ending with svāhā, with 'ṛc and sāman…'.
There is no conflicting soma sacrifice (asaṃsava) when there is an intervention of a great mountain, a great river, a chariot's day-journey, or the wind;
some say, merely from the absence of mutual hostility.

1.11.s: hutvā japeyurbrahmāhaṃ gāyatrīṃ vācaṃ prāṇaṃ prajāpatiṃ prapadye'śmānamākhaṇaṃ paryūha iti
1.11.d: हुत्वा जपेयुर्ब्रह्माहं गायत्रीं वाचं प्राणं प्रजापतिं प्रपद्येऽश्मानमाखणं पर्यूह इति
1.11.m: Having offered, they should murmur: 'I, the brahman, resort to the gāyatrī, to speech, to breath, to Prajāpati; push around the target-stone…'.
Gliding forth, they should turn following the adhvaryu priest.

1.11.s: savyaiḥ pāṇibhiḥ pṛthagdakṣiṇā tṛṇāni nirasyeyuryo'dyasaumya iti
1.11.d: सव्यैः पाणिभिः पृथग्दक्षिणा तृणानि निरस्येयुर्योऽद्यसौम्य इति
1.11.m: With their left hands they should cast away grass blades individually toward the south with 'He who today, being of Soma…'.
Having reached the place of the pit (cātvāla), when the adhvaryu priest has sat down, they should sit down to the west of him with 'He who is my self…'.
The prastotṛ priest faces west.
The pratihārtṛ priest, having gone behind the udgātṛ priest, [sits] looking towards the south-eastern eighth-direction.

1.11.s: savyādharānupasthān kṛtvā dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ sandhimīkṣamāṇāḥ samāni mukhāni dhārayantaḥ
1.11.d: सव्याधरानुपस्थान् कृत्वा द्यावापृथिव्योः सन्धिमीक्षमाणाः समानि मुखानि धारयन्तः
1.11.m: Having placed their left laps below, looking at the junction of heaven and earth, holding their faces level.
Thus they should sit during all stotras.
West of the udgātṛ priests [sit] the chorus-singers, at least three in number;
some say at least four.

1.11.s: ta etenākṣareṇopagāyeyurho iti mandrasvareṇa santataṃ sahavācyeṣvāramantaḥ
1.11.d: त एतेनाक्षरेणोपगायेयुर्हो इति मन्द्रस्वरेण सन्ततं सहवाच्येष्वारमन्तः
1.11.m: They should accompany the singing with this syllable, "ho", in a low tone, continuously, pausing at the places where [words] are to be spoken together.
They should praise with an interval of three [tones] from that [accompanying sound].
Or on the same [tone] at the morning pressing.

1.12.s: prastaraṃ pratigṛhya prastotā brahmstoṣyāmaḥ praśāstarityudgātre prayacchet
1.12.d: प्रस्तरं प्रतिगृह्य प्रस्तोता ब्रह्म्स्तोष्यामः प्रशास्तरित्युद्गात्रे प्रयच्छेत्
1.12.m: Having received the grass clump, the prastotṛ priest should hand it to the udgātṛ priest, saying: "O Brahman, we shall praise; O director!"
Touching his right shin with it, he should yoke the stoma with: "By the splendor of Agni..."
He should whisper: "I will make food."
They should silently look toward the cātvāla trench and the water vessel.
[He should look] at the sun with: "You are the sāman, shine toward me!"
Having produced the hiṅkāra syllable once, they should praise with the bahiṣpavamāna chant.
The first verse of the seminal verses is without the hiṅkāra syllable.

The final one has the form of the Rathantara, with its hiṅkāra syllable emitted.

After its prastāva, he should insert four syllables of stobha.
Having praised, he should whisper: "I have made food."
He should have the patron of the sacrifice say over the grass clump: "You are a falcon..."
Everywhere, having praised, they should invite one another.
Looking at the spectators and fellow officiants, he should whisper: "With splendor..."
[He should look] at the sun with: "Homage to the Gandharva..."
Even if it is concealed by the terrain.
He should perform all this at the two subsequent pavamāna chants.
However, the invocations of ancestry cease, as does [the sequence] beginning with looking at the cātvāla trench up to the hiṅkāra syllable.
And at the third pressing, the entering and cleansing are omitted.

1.12.s: kumbhantu tatra sammṛjyāduttare havirdhāne yaḥ pūrvo droṇakalaśāvṛtā
1.12.d: कुम्भन्तु तत्र सम्मृज्यादुत्तरे हविर्धाने यः पूर्वो द्रोणकलशावृता
1.12.m: There, however, he should cleanse the jar which is the eastern one in the northern havirdhāna shed, following the procedure for the droṇakalaśa.
They call that one the pūtabhṛt; they call that one the pūtabhṛt.

2.1.s: stomayoge'gniryunaktvītyatasya sthāne vāyuryunakta sūryo yunaktviti nānāsavanayoḥ
2.1.d: स्तोमयोगेऽग्निर्युनक्त्वीत्यतस्य स्थाने वायुर्युनक्त सूर्यो युनक्त्विति नानासवनयोः
2.1.m: At the yoking of the stoma, instead of "May Agni yoke...", there are "May Vāyu yoke..." and "May Sūrya yoke..." at the different soma-pressing sessions.

2.1.s: vihāraṃ dhānañjayyo'gnestejasā bṛhaspatistveti prātaḥsavana indriyasyendriyeṇa bṛhaspatistveti mādhyandine sūryasyeti tṛtīyasavane
2.1.d: विहारं धानञ्जय्योऽग्नेस्तेजसा बृहस्पतिस्त्वेति प्रातःसवन इन्द्रियस्येन्द्रियेण बृहस्पतिस्त्वेति माध्यन्दिने सूर्यस्येति तृतीयसवने
2.1.m: Dhānañjayya [prescribes] the variation: "By the splendor of Agni, may Bṛhaspati [yoke] you..." at the morning pressing; "By the power of Indra's power, may Bṛhaspati [yoke] you..." at the midday pressing; and "Of Sūrya..." at the third pressing.
At the recitation by the patron of the sacrifice, [the formulas are] "You are a bull..." and "You are the tone..."

2.1.s: stutvā bahiṣpavamānena prastarādubhayataścaturaṅgulaṃ parichidya tṛṇaṃ cātvāle pravidhyedyadi stutaṃ yadi vādya suṣṭutamarvāk stutaṃ yadi vātiṣṭutaṃ yattayoranyena divamā ruhememamanyena jayema lokamiti
2.1.d: स्तुत्वा बहिष्पवमानेन प्रस्तरादुभयतश्चतुरङ्गुलं परिछिद्य तृणं चात्वाले प्रविध्येद्यदि स्तुतं यदि वाद्य सुष्टुतमर्वाक् स्तुतं यदि वातिष्टुतं यत्तयोरन्येन दिवमा रुहेमेममन्येन जयेम लोकमिति
2.1.m: Having praised with the bahiṣpavamāna chant, having cut off four finger-breadths from both ends of the grass clump, he should cast the blade of grass into the cātvāla trench with: "Whether praised or well-praised today, whether under-praised or over-praised, by one of the two may we ascend to heaven, by the other may we conquer this world!"

2.1.s: tatraivodapātraṃ ninayeyuḥ samudraṃ vaḥ prahiṇomi svāṃ yonimabhigacchatāriṣṭāstanvo bhūyāḥ sma māparā seci no dhanamiti
2.1.d: तत्रैवोदपात्रं निनयेयुः समुद्रं वः प्रहिणोमि स्वां योनिमभिगच्छतारिष्टास्तन्वो भूयाः स्म मापरा सेचि नो धनमिति
2.1.m: In that very place they should pour out the water vessel with: "I send you to the ocean; go to your own womb! Unharmed may our bodies be; may our wealth not be poured away!"
Outside the altar, facing north, they should stride an odd number of steps, fewer than ten.
Having approached the Āgnīdhra fire, they should recite the verses of the bahiṣpavamāna chant.

2.1.s: anuvyāhāriṣīnmāmiti yamiti śaṃketa tasmā āgnīdhrīya āhutīvajraṃ praharedyajña śaṃ ca ta upa ca te namaśca te satyo'si satyasaṃskṛtastasya te ya ūnaṃ yo'kṛtaṃ yo'tiriktamadarśattasya prāṇenāpyāyasva svāheti
2.1.d: अनुव्याहारिषीन्मामिति यमिति शंकेत तस्मा आग्नीध्रीय आहुतीवज्रं प्रहरेद्यज्ञ शं च त उप च ते नमश्च ते सत्योऽसि सत्यसंस्कृतस्तस्य ते य ऊनं योऽकृतं योऽतिरिक्तमदर्शत्तस्य प्राणेनाप्यायस्व स्वाहेति
2.1.m: If he suspects someone, thinking "He might utter a curse against me," he should strike a thunderbolt of an oblation into the Āgnīdhra fire against him, with: "O sacrifice, peace to you, homage to you, reverence to you! You are truth, consecrated by truth. Whoever saw what is deficient in you, what is unperformed, what is redundant—replenish yourself with his breath of life, svāhā!"
Dhānañjayya says: "One must not deviate [from this rule]."

2.2.m: They should praise in the sadas with the bahiṣpavamāna chants of an ahīna, except on the first day.
Stepping out before the distribution of the dhiṣṇya hearths, they should conclude [the rites] beginning with the casting of the blade of grass.
Gautama says that in the three-day rite of the Veda, the rule of the sacrificial session applies.
Dhānañjayya says that the rule of the ahīna applies.
They should praise in a low tone at the morning pressing, and progressively higher at the subsequent two.
At this time they should eat.

2.2.s: anusavanantu satreṣu savanamukhīyān bhakṣayitvā sanneṣu nārāśseṣu
2.2.d: अनुसवनन्तु सत्रेषु सवनमुखीयान् भक्षयित्वा सन्नेषु नाराश्सेषु
2.2.m: At each pressing in sacrificial sessions, however, having consumed the initial pressing portions, when the Nārāśaṃsa cups are deposited.
When the omentum has been offered, they should pay reverence to the dhiṣṇya hearths.

2.2.s: cātvāle tu mārjanaṃ pūrv satreṣvidamāpaḥ pravahatāvadyañca malañca yadyaccābhidudrohānṛtaṃ yacca śepe abhīruṇamāpo mā tasmādenaso duritātpāntu viśvato nirmā muñcāmi śapathānnirmā varuṇāduta nirmā yamasya ṣaḍvśiātsarvasmādeva kilbiṣāt sumitriyā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu durmitriyāstasmai santu yo'smān dveṣṭi yañca vayandviṣma iti
2.2.d: चात्वाले तु मार्जनं पूर्व् सत्रेष्विदमापः प्रवहतावद्यञ्च मलञ्च यद्यच्चाभिदुद्रोहानृतं यच्च शेपे अभीरुणमापो मा तस्मादेनसो दुरितात्पान्तु विश्वतो निर्मा मुञ्चामि शपथान्निर्मा वरुणादुत निर्मा यमस्य षड्व्शिआत्सर्वस्मादेव किल्बिषात् सुमित्रिया न आप ओषधयः सन्तु दुर्मित्रियास्तस्मै सन्तु योऽस्मान् द्वेष्टि यञ्च वयन्द्विष्म इति

2.2.m: Having attended upon the Āhavanīya fire with "You are the sovereign ruler...", and having turned north past the āstāva ground, the cātvāla trench, and the Śāmitra hearth, facing north [they revere it] with: "Praised, wiped clean by the sky!"
They should attend upon the Āgnīdhra fire with: "You are all-pervading..."
Everywhere the passage is to the north of it.
At the two subsequent pressings, [the passage is] to the south when [they approach] the havirdhāna shed and the Āhavanīya fire for the pṛṣṭha oblation.
Standing at the eastern door of the sadas, facing west, [they revere] the Hotṛ's dhiṣṇya hearth with: "The conveyer..."
[They revere] that of the Maitrāvaruṇa with: "Invigorating..."
Facing north, [they revere] those of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin and following priests with: "Tutha...", "Desirous...", "Anghāri...", and "Seeking aid..."
Standing right there, [they revere] the Mārjālīya hearth with: "The purifier..."
[They revere] the post of udumbara wood with: 'O thou of true domain!'
The seat of the brahman priest with: 'O ocean!'
Having gone to the north of the sadas, standing inside the sacrificial enclosure facing west, [they revere] the prajahita fire with: 'O serpent!'
The place of the dakṣiṇāgni fire with: 'O full of waves!'
The southern edge of the altar with: 'O wise one!'

2.2.s: tatraiva tiṣṭhantaḥ sarvān samanvīkṣamāṇāḥ pāta meti
2.2.d: तत्रैव तिष्ठन्तः सर्वान् समन्वीक्षमाणाः पात मेति
2.2.m: Standing right there and looking at all of them together, [they say]: 'Protect me!'
Śāṇḍilya says that they should say this having revered each one individually, turning the plural words into singular ones.

2.3.m: If they should perform the rites according to the Rauruki tradition, they should first revere the sun with: 'Of paths…'

2.3.s: āhavanīyamupasthāya tamevāpi jo'si jāyamāna ityapi jo'si navajāta iti vā yamagnimanupraharanti tamabhipretya
2.3.d: आहवनीयमुपस्थाय तमेवापि जोऽसि जायमान इत्यपि जोऽसि नवजात इति वा यमग्निमनुप्रहरन्ति तमभिप्रेत्य
2.3.m: Having revered the āhavanīya fire, having approached the fire which they throw along with [the formula], [they revere] that very fire with: 'Thou art born from the waters when being born', or with: 'Thou art born from the waters when newly born.'
When [they revere] the cātvāla pit, then [they revere] the heap of rubbish with: 'Thou art the uproarious one making a roar.'
When [they revere] the slaughtering-place, then [they revere] the place where they bury the entrails with: 'Thou art the earth-born keeper of the entrails.'

2.3.s: yadāgnīdhrīyamatha yatrācchāvāka āsīnohotaryupahavamicchatyupahavyo'si namasya ityupahavyo'si tanūpā iti vā
2.3.d: यदाग्नीध्रीयमथ यत्राच्छावाक आसीनोहोतर्युपहवमिच्छत्युपहव्योऽसि नमस्य इत्युपहव्योऽसि तनूपा इति वा
2.3.m: When [they revere] the āgnīdhra shed, then [they revere] the place where the acchāvāka priest, being seated, seeks an invitation with the formula 'O Hotṛ…', with: 'Thou art worthy of invitation, venerable!' or with: 'Thou art worthy of invitation, body-protecting!'

2.3.s: yadā brahmaṇaḥ sadanamatha sadasyasya sadasyo'si malimluca iti
2.3.d: यदा ब्रह्मणः सदनमथ सदस्यस्य सदस्योऽसि मलिम्लुच इति
2.3.m: When [they revere] the seat of the brahman priest, then [they revere that] of the sadasya priest with: 'Thou art the sadasya, the interloper.'

2.3.s: yadā dakṣiṇaṃ vedyantamatha prājāpatyamasīti patnīśālāmaindramasīti sado vaiṣṇavamasīti havirddhānamaindrāgnamasītyāgnīdhrīyaṃ vaiśvadevamasīti vā
2.3.d: यदा दक्षिणं वेद्यन्तमथ प्राजापत्यमसीति पत्नीशालामैन्द्रमसीति सदो वैष्णवमसीति हविर्द्धानमैन्द्राग्नमसीत्याग्नीध्रीयं वैश्वदेवमसीति वा
2.3.m: When [they revere] the southern edge of the altar, then [they revere] the wife's hall with: 'Thou belongest to Prajāpati', the sadas with: 'Thou belongest to Indra', the cart-shed with: 'Thou belongest to Viṣṇu', the āgnīdhra shed with: 'Thou belongest to Indrāgni', or [they revere it] with: 'Thou belongest to the Viśve Devas.'

2.3.s: atha tathaiva samastena sarve stha somyāsaḥ sarve somaṃ pibata sarve somasya pītimānaśadhve pāta meti samānaṃ param
2.3.d: अथ तथैव समस्तेन सर्वे स्थ सोम्यासः सर्वे सोमं पिबत सर्वे सोमस्य पीतिमानशध्वे पात मेति समानं परम्
2.3.m: Then in the same manner, with the collective [formula]: 'You are all soma-loving; drink, all of you, the soma; you have all attained the drinking of soma; protect me!' The remainder is the same.

2.3.s: ṛtasya dvārau stha ityaparau dvārabāhū saṃmṛjya mā mā santāptamiti praviśeyuḥ
2.3.d: ऋतस्य द्वारौ स्थ इत्यपरौ द्वारबाहू संमृज्य मा मा सन्ताप्तमिति प्रविशेयुः
2.3.m: Having wiped the two western door-posts with: 'You two are the doors of the cosmic order', they should enter with: 'Do not burn me!'

2.3.s: dakṣiṇenaudumbarīṃ gatvā tasyā uttarata upaviśeyurnamaḥ sakhibhyaḥ iti
2.3.d: दक्षिणेनौदुम्बरीं गत्वा तस्या उत्तरत उपविशेयुर्नमः सखिभ्यः इति
2.3.m: Having gone south of the post of udumbara wood, they should sit down to the north of it with: 'Homage to the companions!'
At this [moment], the pratihārtṛ priest should walk in front of the prastotṛ priest.
At this time they should invite one another.
They should perform all this, beginning from the wiping of the door-posts, whenever they revere the dhiṣṇya hearths.
If the udgātṛ priest should perform the role of the patron of the sacrifice or of the brahman priest, he should revere the āgnīdhra shed and step around to the east.
Having revered the dhiṣṇya hearths belonging to the sadas, looking from there alone [he reveres] those belonging to the wife's hall.

2.4.s: ṛtasya dvārau stha iti pūrvau dvārabāhū saṃmṛjya dakṣiṇasya purastādudaṅmukha upaviśediti dhānañjayyaḥ
2.4.d: ऋतस्य द्वारौ स्थ इति पूर्वौ द्वारबाहू संमृज्य दक्षिणस्य पुरस्तादुदङ्मुख उपविशेदिति धानञ्जय्यः
2.4.m: Dhānañjayya says that having wiped the two eastern door-posts with: 'You two are the doors of the cosmic order', he should sit down in front of the southern one, facing north.
The entering and sitting down have been explained.
Having gone along the path of the priests, [the procedure] beginning with the collective reverence is the same.

2.4.s: dakṣiṇārddhe tu sadasaḥ pūrvamupaveśanaṃ prastotuḥ pratyupaveśanaṃ brahmopaveśanena nirastaḥ parāvasuriti dakṣiṇātṛṇaṃ nirasyedāvasoḥ sadane sīdāmītyupaviśet
2.4.d: दक्षिणार्द्धे तु सदसः पूर्वमुपवेशनं प्रस्तोतुः प्रत्युपवेशनं ब्रह्मोपवेशनेन निरस्तः परावसुरिति दक्षिणातृणं निरस्येदावसोः सदने सीदामीत्युपविशेत्
2.4.m: In the southern half of the sadas, however, the sitting down of the prastotṛ priest is first; the counter-sitting is by means of the sitting of the brahman priest; he should cast away a blade of grass toward the south with: 'Expelled is Parāvasu', [and] he should sit down with: 'I sit in the seat of the benevolent one.'
Having said: 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Bṛhaspati is the brahman priest; I am human', having gone to the post of udumbara wood, he should sit down.
In this order he should endeavor to perform everything according to the seat.
If he should become exhausted, [he should sit] right upon [a seat near] the post of udumbara wood.
The sadasya priest, revering the dhiṣṇya hearths in this very way, should enter after the brahman priest or the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin priest.
His mutual invitation should be with that one, and the consumption [of soma] should be shared.
If they should feel loathing, there should be separate cups.
When [the priests] glide, he should leave the sadas empty.
His ritual action ends with the consumption of curd.

2.4.s: vissthite savane pūrvayā dvārāntareṇa hoturdhiṣṇyaṃ maitrāvaruṇasya ca sañcaraḥ
2.4.d: विस्स्थिते सवने पूर्वया द्वारान्तरेण होतुर्धिष्ण्यं मैत्रावरुणस्य च सञ्चरः
2.4.m: When the pressing session has concluded, the movement of the hotṛ priest and the maitrāvaruṇa priest is through the eastern door, between the dhiṣṇya hearths.
As they came, so they go; as they came, so they go.

2.5.s: camasaṃ pratigṛhya prastotā dakṣiṇa ūrāvādhāya dakṣiṇena pāṇināpidhāyāsīta
2.5.d: चमसं प्रतिगृह्य प्रस्तोता दक्षिण ऊरावाधाय दक्षिणेन पाणिनापिधायासीत
2.5.m: Having received the cup, having placed it on his right thigh and having covered it with his right hand, the prastotṛ priest should remain seated.
While the iḍā is being invoked, he should touch [the cup] subsequently, without striking [it].
Everywhere, after the vaṣaṭ-maker's consumption, they should consume [their soma], having mutually invited one another.

2.5.s: dakṣiṇamanu bāhundaṇḍe kṛtvā śyena ityavekṣyendaviti dviralpaṃ bhakṣayedyathāsavanaṃ chandāsyādiśan
2.5.d: दक्षिणमनु बाहुन्दण्डे कृत्वा श्येन इत्यवेक्ष्येन्दविति द्विरल्पं भक्षयेद्यथासवनं छन्दास्यादिशन्

2.5.s: ūrddhva iti mukhyān prāṇānabhimṛśeta soma rārandhīti hṛdayaṃ somagīrbhiriti nābhim
2.5.d: ऊर्द्ध्व इति मुख्यान् प्राणानभिमृशेत सोम रारन्धीति हृदयं सोमगीर्भिरिति नाभिम्
2.5.m: With: 'Upward…', he should touch the principal breaths; with: 'O Soma, delight…', the heart; with: 'With the somas, by songs…', the navel.
Touching the handle, he should swell [the cup] with: 'Swell…'
Or all [swell it] with this gāyatrī verse.

2.5.s: tāṃ tṛtīyasavane dvirbrūyuḥ sante payāsīti mādhyandine
2.5.d: तां तृतीयसवने द्विर्ब्रूयुः सन्ते पयासीति माध्यन्दिने
2.5.m: They should say it twice at the third pressing session; at the midday pressing session with: 'May thy milk-juices gather together…'
Śāṇḍilya says that the swelling is with the gāyatrī verse alone at each pressing session.
The second [portions of soma] at the pressing sessions belong to the Narāśaṃsa [praises], and the third [portions] at the first two [pressing sessions].

2.5.s: teṣāmanavekṣya bhakṣaṇamavamairiti prātaḥsavana aurbairiti mādhyandine kāvyairiti tṛtīyasavane
2.5.d: तेषामनवेक्ष्य भक्षणमवमैरिति प्रातःसवन और्बैरिति माध्यन्दिने काव्यैरिति तृतीयसवने
2.5.m: Their consumption [is done] without looking down: with 'by the lowest [fathers]' at the morning pressing, with 'by the Urva [fathers]' at the midday pressing, [and] with 'by the Kāvya [fathers]' at the third pressing.
He should everywhere add: 'along with the fathers.'
Regarding the re-touching, [it may be done] as one pleases.
He should replenish the first and second [cups] at the previous two soma-pressing sessions; the first at the third pressing.

2.5.s: āvarttiṣu tṛṇe pratigṛhya prastotā prayacchedyathā prastaram
2.5.d: आवर्त्तिषु तृणे प्रतिगृह्य प्रस्तोता प्रयच्छेद्यथा प्रस्तरम्
2.5.m: At the turns, having received two grass-blades, the prastotṛ priest should hand [them] over like the prastara.
If they are not brought, he should not omit the formula.

2.5.s: tathaiva jaṅghāmupahatya yuñjyāt stomandīkṣāyai tapaso manaso vāca iti nānā dhānañjayyo yatrānantarāṇi catvāri
2.5.d: तथैव जङ्घामुपहत्य युञ्ज्यात् स्तोमन्दीक्षायै तपसो मनसो वाच इति नाना धानञ्जय्यो यत्रानन्तराणि चत्वारि
2.5.m: In that very way, striking the shank, he should yoke the stoma with 'To consecration, to heat, to mind, to speech,' severally, according to Dhānañjayya, where there are four continuous [stomas].
At the end of all [he adds]: 'May Prajāpati [yoke] you.'
In smaller [numbers of stomas], the subsequent one should be omitted each time.
He should yoke the Vājapeya-sāman with the first.
Likewise in the surplus stotras.
On the day of preparation, they should not chant.

2.6.s: prastotā tu kuśāḥ kārayedyajñiyasya vṛkṣasya khadirasya dīrghasatreṣveke prādeśamātrīḥ kuśāḥ pṛṣṭhāstvaktaḥ samāmajjato'ṅguṣṭhaparvapṛthumātrīḥ prajñātāgrāḥ kārayitvā gandhaiḥ pralipya sarpiṣā satreṣveke vaiṣṭutena vasanena pariveṣṭya kṣaumaśāṇakārpāśānāṃ kenaciduparyaudumbaryā vāsayet
2.6.d: प्रस्तोता तु कुशाः कारयेद्यज्ञियस्य वृक्षस्य खदिरस्य दीर्घसत्रेष्वेके प्रादेशमात्रीः कुशाः पृष्ठास्त्वक्तः समामज्जतोऽङ्गुष्ठपर्वपृथुमात्रीः प्रज्ञाताग्राः कारयित्वा गन्धैः प्रलिप्य सर्पिषा सत्रेष्वेके वैष्टुतेन वसनेन परिवेष्ट्य क्षौमशाणकार्पाशानां केनचिदुपर्यौदुम्बर्या वासयेत्
2.6.m: The prastotṛ priest, however, should cause pegs of sacrificial wood to be made—of khadira, some say, in long sacrificial sessions—a span in length, smooth on the bark side, thick as the thumb-joint at the marrow, having marked tops; and having caused them to be made, having smeared them with perfumes and ghee—some say in sacrificial sessions—having wrapped them with the cloth used for counting the stomas, made of linen, hemp, or cotton, he should cause them to rest above the audumbarī pillar.

2.6.s: tā śvo bhūte kuśairūrddhvāgrairveṣṭayitvaivaṃjātīyenaiva vasanena pradakṣiṇamūrddhvadaśena pariveṣṭya spṛṣṭo'napaśrita udgāyet
2.6.d: ता श्वो भूते कुशैरूर्द्ध्वाग्रैर्वेष्टयित्वैवंजातीयेनैव वसनेन प्रदक्षिणमूर्द्ध्वदशेन परिवेष्ट्य स्पृष्टोऽनपश्रित उद्गायेत्
2.6.m: On the next day, having wrapped them with kuśa-blades with upward-pointing tips, having encircled them sunwise with a cloth of that same kind with upward-pointing fringes, [the udgātṛ priest], touched [by the others] and not leaning, should sing the udgītha.
Some say: he may boldly lean.

2.6.s: stoṣyamāṇānāṃ madhye vaiṣṭutaṃ vasanaṃ prāksamāsaṃ vodaksamāsaṃ vā uparidaśamāstīryya prastotā kuśā vidadhyāt prastāvānteṣu
2.6.d: स्तोष्यमाणानां मध्ये वैष्टुतं वसनं प्राक्समासं वोदक्समासं वा उपरिदशमास्तीर्य्य प्रस्तोता कुशा विदध्यात् प्रस्तावान्तेषु
2.6.m: In the middle of those about to chant the stotra, having spread the cloth used for counting the stomas with the fold to the east or with the fold to the north and with the fringe on top, the prastotṛ priest should place the pegs at the ends of the prastāvas;
[He places] the first strophic shift pointing north, positioned to the east or to the west;
to the west of that, pointing east or west, positioned to the north through the middle space;
to the west of that, pointing north, positioned to the west; in this manner are the successive rounds.
He should join together the strophic shifts of a round.
At the beginnings of rounds they should chant with the hiṅkāra syllable.
Having chanted the prastāva of the final [verse], he should look at the praśāstṛ priest, saying: 'This one.'
'Of the chanted thou art chanted' is the patron of the sacrifice's formula.

2.6.s: savanassthāsu praśāstrokto yathetamaparayā dvārā niṣkramya paścimenāgnīdhrīyaṃ bahirvedi mūtraṃ kuryuḥ
2.6.d: सवनस्स्थासु प्रशास्त्रोक्तो यथेतमपरया द्वारा निष्क्रम्य पश्चिमेनाग्नीध्रीयं बहिर्वेदि मूत्रं कुर्युः
2.6.m: When [the verses] abide in the soma-pressing session, being addressed by the praśāstṛ priest, having gone out by the western door as they came, they should pass urine outside the vedi, to the west of the Āgnīdhra fire.
They should restrain their speech until they have rinsed with water.
Along it, they should not go farther than the throw of a yoke-pin.
He who wishes to go farther should go by the well-known [path].

2.7.m: Then, Gautama and Śāṇḍilyāyana say that they should attend upon the dhiṣṇya hearths with the combined [formula] at the two latter soma-pressing sessions.
Dhānañjayya says: with the entire [formula].
Śāṇḍilya says: no attendance.
Having gone out in this very way, they should attend upon the others after the uktha lauds separately from the stotras with the combined [formula];
but after the rounds of the night [sacrifice].
Having sat down according to his seat, the prastotṛ priest should go to the Havirdhāna cart-shed at the midday pressing;
the pratihārtṛ priest at the third pressing when the Āditya cup has been offered;
in sacrificial sessions, all of them at both [times].

2.7.s: pavamānayoruttarayordhiṣṇyaviharaṇe mārjjālīyharantaḥ paścimena yajamānhṛtvā tenaiva pratihareyuḥ
2.7.d: पवमानयोरुत्तरयोर्धिष्ण्यविहरणे मार्ज्जालीय्हरन्तः पश्चिमेन यजमान्हृत्वा तेनैव प्रतिहरेयुः
2.7.m: At the distribution of the dhiṣṇya hearths for the two latter pavamāna chants, carrying the Mārjālīya fire, having carried it behind the patron of the sacrifice, they should carry it back along that same path.

2.7.s: madhyandinena stutvā satreṣu dadhigharmasya bhakṣayeyuḥ samupahūya dadhikrāvṇa iti
2.7.d: मध्यन्दिनेन स्तुत्वा सत्रेषु दधिघर्मस्य भक्षयेयुः समुपहूय दधिक्राव्ण इति
2.7.m: Having chanted with the midday [pavamāna chant], in sacrificial sessions they should consume [their share] of the dadhigharma, having given the ritual invitation, with [the verse beginning with]: 'Of Dadhikrāvan.'
On the tenth day, they should repeat its last verse-quarter.
To the east of the wife's hall and between the Āgnīdhra fire and the sadas, they should lead the priestly gifts along the sacred ford.
For all of them, the recitation beforehand is: 'At the god's [impulse]...'
He should accept them according to the deity with: 'May Varuṇa [give] thee...'
Pairs as masculine, except for she-goats.
With 'Who [has given] this to whom?' is the recitation afterward.

2.7.s: tatrohāpādīni tvā devi dakṣiṇe'da iti ca yattatsyāt tena dātra idamāviśaitatta iti ca bhuñjatīti ca bhūyāddhsiīriti ca
2.7.d: तत्रोहापादीनि त्वा देवि दक्षिणेऽद इति च यत्तत्स्यात् तेन दात्र इदमाविशैतत्त इति च भुञ्जतीति च भूयाद्ध्सिईरिति च

2.7.s: aśvarathañceddadyāt pūrveṇāgnīdhrīyamavasthāpya purastājjapaṃ japitvā darbhamuṣṭināśvamukhāni saṃmṛjyāddvābhyāṃ dvābhyāmaśvanāmabhyāmekaikasyāśvo'sītyetatprabhṛtibhirudakssthamiti dhānañjayyaḥ
2.7.d: अश्वरथञ्चेद्दद्यात् पूर्वेणाग्नीध्रीयमवस्थाप्य पुरस्ताज्जपं जपित्वा दर्भमुष्टिनाश्वमुखानि संमृज्याद्द्वाभ्यां द्वाभ्यामश्वनामभ्यामेकैकस्याश्वोऽसीत्येतत्प्रभृतिभिरुदक्स्स्थमिति धानञ्जय्यः
2.7.m: If he gives a horse-chariot, having halted it to the east of the Āgnīdhra fire, having recited the recitation beforehand, he should wipe the horses' mouths with a handful of darbha grass with two horse-names for each, beginning with 'Thou art a horse,' positioned to the north, according to Dhānañjayya;
another view is: the two yoke-horses first;
Śāṇḍilya says: all [names] on each one, positioned to the north;
These very [formulas] he should adapt appropriately for mares, mules, and she-mules.
If [the gift consists of three animals], [the formula applies] half to one and half to two, or divided equally between two.

2.8.m: Touching the front part of the chariot, he should murmur: 'Of the Ādityas…'
With whatever belongs to a chariot, [namely with the formula:] 'Of Vāyu…', he should accept an object made of leather;
with 'Of the stars…', an object made of bone;

2.8.s: dakṣiṇena rathaṃ gatvā rathantaramasīti dakṣiṇaṃ cakramālabhet
2.8.d: दक्षिणेन रथं गत्वा रथन्तरमसीति दक्षिणं चक्रमालभेत्
2.8.m: Going south of the chariot, he should touch the right wheel with: 'You are the Rathantara.'
The chassis with: 'You are the Vāmadevya.'
The left wheel with: 'You are the Bṛhat.'
With: 'The bends and hooks…', he should wipe the two wheels.
With: 'Vaiśvānara…', he should mount with the right foot.
Having mounted, he should murmur: 'They have sought the cow…'
With: 'Slender…', he should tighten the reins on the left.
With: 'Servant…', he should pull back those on the right.
Having dismounted, having recited the Vāruṇa formula once, and having specified according to the deity, he should murmur the subsequent murmur: thus says Gautama.

2.8.s: saṃmārjanaprabhṛtyetat sarvaṃ kṛtvā vimucya nānā purastājjapopariṣṭājjapau vāruṇamaśvebhyo rathāya ceti dhānañjayyaḥ
2.8.d: संमार्जनप्रभृत्येतत् सर्वं कृत्वा विमुच्य नाना पुरस्ताज्जपोपरिष्टाज्जपौ वारुणमश्वेभ्यो रथाय चेति धानञ्जय्यः
2.8.m: Having performed all this beginning with the wiping, and having unyoked [the horses], there are distinct preceding and subsequent murmurs, and a Vāruṇa formula for the horses and for the chariot: thus says Dhānañjayya.
If he should become exhausted, he may murmur all this while remaining seated.
If he gives a chariot horse, he should murmur the names of the horses before the Vāruṇa formula,
He should accept it with whichever [formula] belongs to a chariot.
Before the Vāruṇa formula for a sheep, [he murmurs the formula:] 'Of food…',
For a garment: 'Knowing, they cut…'
If gold less than what is enjoyable should come [to him], he should attach it to the audumbarī post,
He should accept combined rice and barley in a single rite;
He should accept gifts whose deities are unspecified with [a formula addressed to] Prajāpati.
The sacrificial gifts in a non-sacrifice [are accepted] silently: thus says Dhānañjayya.
'Bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ': thus says Gautama;

2.9.s: pūrvaṃ nārāśaṃsambhakṣayitvāhavanīye prastotā pṛṣṭhahomaṃ juhuyādyatpṛṣṭh syāttadādiśyādaḥ pibatu somyaṃ madhvāyurddadhadyajñapatāvavihrutamimaṃ yajñamabhisaṃvasānā hotrāstṛpyantu sumanasyamānāḥ svāheti pūrvām
2.9.d: पूर्वं नाराशंसम्भक्षयित्वाहवनीये प्रस्तोता पृष्ठहोमं जुहुयाद्यत्पृष्ठ् स्यात्तदादिश्यादः पिबतु सोम्यं मध्वायुर्द्दधद्यज्ञपतावविह्रुतमिमं यज्ञमभिसंवसाना होत्रास्तृप्यन्तु सुमनस्यमानाः स्वाहेति पूर्वाम्
2.9.m: Having consumed the earlier nārāśaṃsa portion, the prastotṛ priest should offer the pṛṣṭha-offering into the āhavanīya fire; specifying whichever pṛṣṭha laud it may be, [he offers] the first [oblation with]: 'May that [pṛṣṭha laud] drink the soma mead, conferring unimpaired lifespan upon the master of the sacrifice; residing together toward this sacrifice, may the Hotrās be gratified, being well-minded, svāhā!'

2.9.s: dvaidhaṃ juhuyāditi dhānañjayyo'daḥ pibatu somyaṃ madhvāyurdadhadyajñapatāvavihrutaṃ svāheti pūrvāmimaṃ yajñamityuttarām
2.9.d: द्वैधं जुहुयादिति धानञ्जय्योऽदः पिबतु सोम्यं मध्वायुर्दधद्यज्ञपतावविह्रुतं स्वाहेति पूर्वामिमं यज्ञमित्युत्तराम्
2.9.m: He should offer [the formula] divided into two, says Dhānañjayya: the first with 'May that [pṛṣṭha laud] drink the soma mead, conferring unimpaired lifespan upon the master of the sacrifice, svāhā!', and the subsequent with 'Toward this sacrifice…'

2.9.s: revatīṣu vāravantīyamiti ṣaṣṭhe pṛṣṭhādeśaṃ gautamo mahāvratamiti vrate
2.9.d: रेवतीषु वारवन्तीयमिति षष्ठे पृष्ठादेशं गौतमो महाव्रतमिति व्रते
2.9.m: Gautama says that on the sixth day the designation of the pṛṣṭha laud is 'the Vāravantīya upon the Revatīs', and at the Mahāvrata rite, 'the Mahāvrata'.

2.9.s: revatyaśca vāravantīyañceti dhānañjayyo yāvanti pṛṣṭhasthāni syuḥ sarvāṇyeva prasañcakṣīta pibatu dadhaditi ca yathārthamūhet
2.9.d: रेवत्यश्च वारवन्तीयञ्चेति धानञ्जय्यो यावन्ति पृष्ठस्थानि स्युः सर्वाण्येव प्रसञ्चक्षीत पिबतु दधदिति च यथार्थमूहेत्
2.9.m: Dhānañjayya says: 'both the Revatīs and the Vāravantīya'; as many as occupy the position of a pṛṣṭha laud, he should mention all of them, and adapt 'may it drink' and 'conferring' according to the sense.

2.9.s: bṛhatā rathantareṇa vā stoṣyamāṇaḥ prāk stomayogāddaśa vyāhṛtīrmanasā dhyāyedairamiti
2.9.d: बृहता रथन्तरेण वा स्तोष्यमाणः प्राक् स्तोमयोगाद्दश व्याहृतीर्मनसा ध्यायेदैरमिति
2.9.m: When about to chant with the Bṛhat or Rathantara, he should mentally meditate on the ten sacred utterances beginning with 'airam' before the yoking of the stoma.
For the Rathantara only, [he meditates also on] the verse: 'What is yours in the cows…'

2.9.s: yuktvā stomametad brūyāditi śāṇḍilya ṛcaṃ pūrvyaṃ vyāhṛtibhya iti
2.9.d: युक्त्वा स्तोममेतद् ब्रूयादिति शाण्डिल्य ऋचं पूर्व्यं व्याहृतिभ्य इति
2.9.m: Śāṇḍilya says that having yoked the stoma, he should recite this, placing the verse prior to the sacred utterances.
When the Rathantara is being introduced by the prastotṛ priest, he should close his eyes completely in all places.
He should mentally connect each syllable with stobhas uttered by speech: with first vowels, with the letter 'a', preceded by 'bh' and other [consonants], not overrun, ending with the second vowel.
They call this 'in accordance with traditional study'.
Leaving four syllables before the pratihāra, he should look up at that point everywhere.
If it is not a pṛṣṭha laud, its special ritual rules cease.
Together with the stobhas: thus says Gautama.
The stobhas alone should follow: thus says Dhānañjayya.
Śāṇḍilya says that he should add the stobhas to what is not a pṛṣṭha laud only in the case of the Agniṣṭomasāman and the Sandhisāman.
The elder Gautama says that he should add the stobhas everywhere to what does not belong to the strophic verse.

2.10.s: vāmadevyena stoṣyamāṇaḥ prāk stomayogādgāvo aśvā ajāvayo vrīhayo yavā iti manasā dhyāyet
2.10.d: वामदेव्येन स्तोष्यमाणः प्राक् स्तोमयोगाद्गावो अश्वा अजावयो व्रीहयो यवा इति मनसा ध्यायेत्
2.10.m: When about to chant with the Vāmadevya, he should mentally meditate before the yoking of the stoma: 'Cows, horses, goats and sheep, rice, barley.'

2.10.s: brahmasāmni yaḥ kāmo yajamānasya syāt sa sidhyatviti dhyāyannupāsīta
2.10.d: ब्रह्मसाम्नि यः कामो यजमानस्य स्यात् स सिध्यत्विति ध्यायन्नुपासीत
2.10.m: During the Brahmasāman, he should sit reverently, meditating: 'Whatever desire the patron of the sacrifice may have, may it be fulfilled!'

2.10.s: ārbhaveṇa stutvā puroḍāśādekaikaṃ piṇḍantrīstrīnvāparayā dvārā havirddhānaṃ prapadyādhastāt svasya camasasya kuryuryadāsannaḥ syādatra pitaro mādayadhvaṃ yathā bhāgamāvṛṣāyadhvamiti
2.10.d: आर्भवेण स्तुत्वा पुरोडाशादेकैकं पिण्डन्त्रीस्त्रीन्वापरया द्वारा हविर्द्धानं प्रपद्याधस्तात् स्वस्य चमसस्य कुर्युर्यदासन्नः स्यादत्र पितरो मादयध्वं यथा भागमावृषायध्वमिति
2.10.m: Having praised with the ārbhava chant, they should enter the havirdhāna shed by the rear door, taking one lump each, or three each, from the sacrificial cake, and place it beneath their own cups when it is deposited, [saying]: 'Here, O fathers, rejoice; act like bulls, each according to his share!'
As it is being brought out, they should address it with the mantra: 'The fathers have rejoiced; they have acted like bulls, each according to his share.'
The udgātṛ priest should look upon the brought soma with: 'My lifespan, my breath…'
[The formula] ends with 'again we place in ourselves' (punar asmāsu dadhmasi).
On the tenth day, they should repeat it.
Having placed his thumb and ring finger in it, he should wipe his two eyes with: 'By which [he won] the contest...' (yenā hy ājim).
They should carry it to the north of the pratihārtṛ priest.
At the hiṅkāra of the yajñāyajñīya, the udgātṛ priest should look towards the wife.
At the cadence, the wife should sprinkle her right thigh.

2.10.s: tṛtīyāyāṃ stotrīyāyāṃ prastutāyāṃ sarvaṃ tadudakaṃ ninayet
2.10.d: तृतीयायां स्तोत्रीयायां प्रस्तुतायां सर्वं तदुदकं निनयेत्
2.10.m: When the third strophic verse is introduced by the prastotṛ priest, she should pour out all that water.

2.10.s: uttamāyāṃ stotrīyāyāṃ bhuvadvājāyi bhuvadvājeṣvityabhyasyennāmiti ca nidhanamanuṣṭubhamuttamāmakṣareṇāntata iti hyāheti
2.10.d: उत्तमायां स्तोत्रीयायां भुवद्वाजायि भुवद्वाजेष्वित्यभ्यस्येन्नामिति च निधनमनुष्टुभमुत्तमामक्षरेणान्तत इति ह्याहेति
2.10.m: On the final strophic verse, he should repeat: 'bhuvad vājāyi, bhuvad vājeṣu' and 'nām' as the cadence; for it says: 'an anuṣṭubh as the final [verse] with a syllable at the end.'
However, the teachers [prescribe] non-repetition, and Śāṇḍilya says that the cadence should be as handed down in the tradition.
Then, when the directed hotṛ priest recites the verses to the waters (āpohiṣṭhīyā), uncovering [themselves], they should take hold of him from behind.
When it has gone to another position, its ritual attributes cease.
They would belong to whatever else might be the agniṣṭoma-sāman.
In the absence of the hiṅkāra, however, the udgātṛ priest should look towards the wife at the time of the pratihāra.
According to the Brāhmaṇa, he should make adaptations based on the verse collection everywhere, even in another sāman.

2.11.s: tṛtīyasavane sarveṣu stotreṣu samāpteṣu bhakṣayitvā stomaṃ vimuñceyurṛtasya tveti
2.11.d: तृतीयसवने सर्वेषु स्तोत्रेषु समाप्तेषु भक्षयित्वा स्तोमं विमुञ्चेयुरृतस्य त्वेति
2.11.m: At the third pressing, when all the stotras are completed, having consumed [their portions], they should release the stoma with: 'Thee of the cosmic order...' (ṛtasya tvā).
With their right hands, they should entangle the kuśa blades.

2.11.s: yajamānavācanādanantaramatra vā yajamānaṃ vācayettantavemā jyotiṣetyasāvanu mā tanuhi jyotiṣeti yathājyeṣṭhaṃ putrāṇāṃ nāmāni gṛhṇīyāt
2.11.d: यजमानवाचनादनन्तरमत्र वा यजमानं वाचयेत्तन्तवेमा ज्योतिषेत्यसावनु मा तनुहि ज्योतिषेति यथाज्येष्ठं पुत्राणां नामानि गृह्णीयात्
2.11.m: Immediately after the reciting of formulas for the patron of the sacrifice, or here, he should make the patron of the sacrifice recite: 'For the offspring, these with light...' (tantave 'mā jyotiṣā), 'O so-and-so, extend me with light' (asāv anu mā tanuhi jyotiṣā); he should mention the names of his sons in order of seniority.
[He says] 'those who are to be born' (janiṣyamāṇāḥ) in the case of unborn [sons].
In sacrificial sessions, whether they are born or unborn, [he says] simply 'sons' (putrāḥ).

2.11.s: vaṣaṭkṛte hāriyojanasya yathetamaparayā dvārā niṣkrāmanto japeyuḥ somehīti
2.11.d: वषट्कृते हारियोजनस्य यथेतमपरया द्वारा निष्क्रामन्तो जपेयुः सोमेहीति
2.11.m: When the vaṣaṭ-call is made for the hāriyojana cup, as they step out together through the western door, they should whisper: 'Come, O Soma' (soma ehi).
They should attend upon the sun with: 'Thou art well-born' (subhūr asi).
If it has set, [they attend upon] the gārhapatya fire.

2.11.s: āgnīdhrīye dve āhutī juhuyurapāṃ puṣpamiti pūrvāṃ svāhākāreṇottarām
2.11.d: आग्नीध्रीये द्वे आहुती जुहुयुरपां पुष्पमिति पूर्वां स्वाहाकारेणोत्तराम्
2.11.m: In the āgnīdhra fire they should offer two oblations: the former with 'flower of the waters' (apāṃ puṣpam), and the latter with the svāhā-call.

2.11.s: hāriyojanyo nāma dhānā droṇakalaśe bhavanti tāsāmudgātā prathama ādadānaḥ samupahūtā bhakṣayiṣyāma iti brūyāt
2.11.d: हारियोजन्यो नाम धाना द्रोणकलशे भवन्ति तासामुद्गाता प्रथम आददानः समुपहूता भक्षयिष्याम इति ब्रूयात्
2.11.m: There are parched barley grains named 'belonging to the hāriyojana' in the wooden tub (droṇakalaśa); taking them first, the udgātṛ priest should say: 'Invited together, we will consume.'

2.11.s: unnetaryupahavamiṣṭvā hāriyojanasya ta iti tirohnyasyetyatirātre yathādhītaṃ vā sarvatra dvirupaghrāya paścādāhavanīyasyāntaḥparidhi nivapeyuḥ
2.11.d: उन्नेतर्युपहवमिष्ट्वा हारियोजनस्य त इति तिरोह्न्यस्येत्यतिरात्रे यथाधीतं वा सर्वत्र द्विरुपघ्राय पश्चादाहवनीयस्यान्तःपरिधि निवपेयुः
2.11.m: Having sought invitation from the unnetṛ priest, with 'of the hāriyojana, thine...' (hāriyojanasya te), or at the atirātra sacrifice with 'of the preserved overnight...' (tiroahnyasya), or everywhere as studied, having smelled them twice, they should scatter them behind the āhavanīya fire within the enclosing sticks.
When [the enclosing sticks] have been thrown after [into the fire, they scatter them] on the edge of the ashes.
Having touched water, they should throw eight chips of wood each into the āhavanīya fire with the formulas beginning with 'Of what is done by gods...' (devakṛtasya) and ending in the sound 'i'.
Śaucivṛkṣi says [he should throw] all of them at once with the last [formula].

2.11.s: apsuṣomā nāma camasāścātvāladeśe'dbhiḥ pūrṇāsteṣu haritāni tṛṇāni prāstāni bhavanti
2.11.d: अप्सुषोमा नाम चमसाश्चात्वालदेशेऽद्भिः पूर्णास्तेषु हरितानि तृणानि प्रास्तानि भवन्ति
2.11.m: There are cups named apsuṣoma in the area of the pit (cātvāla), filled with water; green grasses are cast into them.

2.11.s: taṃ svaṃ camasaṃ paryupaviśyāpsu dhautetyavamṛśya japeyuḥ
2.11.d: तं स्वं चमसं पर्युपविश्याप्सु धौतेत्यवमृश्य जपेयुः
2.11.m: Having sat around their respective cup and touched it, they should whisper: 'Washed in the waters...' (apsu dhauta).
With 'possessing sweetness...' (madhumantam) they should smell their hands.
With 'desire...' (kāma) they should turn it towards themselves.
With 'nourishment...' (ūrk) they should place their hands on their chests.
With 'breath, O Soma...' (prāṇa soma) they should touch the principal breaths [at the sensory orifices of the head].

2.11.s: āgnīdhrīyaṃ gatvā dadhibhakṣaṃ bhakṣayeyurasamupahūya dadhikrāvṇa iti
2.11.d: आग्नीध्रीयं गत्वा दधिभक्षं भक्षयेयुरसमुपहूय दधिक्राव्ण इति
2.11.m: Having gone to the āgnīdhra fire, they should consume the curd portion without mutual invitation, with: 'Of Dadhikrāvan...' (dadhikrāvṇaḥ).

2.12.m: 'Agni shines...' (agniṣ ṭapati) is the concluding purificatory bath chant.
Its procedure is like that of the first pravargya chant.
All the officiating priests should join in the cadence.
The iṣṭāhotrīya melody is used at the royal consecration rite (abhiṣecanīya).
In the horse-sacrifice three-day rite (aśvatrirātra), the days have separate concluding purificatory baths.
Of these, for the first day, 'From of old, O Agni...' (sanād agne) is the concluding purificatory bath chant.

2.12.s: yadvā u viśpatiriti dvitīyasya tyagnāyiriti vā
2.12.d: यद्वा उ विश्पतिरिति द्वितीयस्य त्यग्नायिरिति वा
2.12.m: For the second, 'Or indeed the lord of the clan...' (yad vā u viśpatiḥ), or 'tyagnāyi...'

2.12.s: avabhṛtheṣṭau saṃsthitāyāmavabhṛtha nicuṃpuṇa nicerurasi nicuṃpuṇāvadevairdevakṛtamenoyāsiṣamava martyairmartyakṛtaṃ pururāvṇo devariṣaspāhītyapa upaspṛśya trirabhyukṣeran
2.12.d: अवभृथेष्टौ संस्थितायामवभृथ निचुंपुण निचेरुरसि निचुंपुणावदेवैर्देवकृतमेनोयासिषमव मर्त्यैर्मर्त्यकृतं पुरुराव्णो देवरिषस्पाहीत्यप उपस्पृश्य त्रिरभ्युक्षेरन्
2.12.m: When the concluding purificatory offering is completed, having touched the water with 'O concluding purificatory bath, Nicumpuṇa! Thou art Niceru, O Nicumpuṇa! May I have wiped away by the gods the sin done against the gods, and by mortals that done against mortals; protect me, O god, from harm caused by the deceitful' (avabhṛtha nicuṃpuṇa...), they should sprinkle themselves three times.

2.12.s: ādityamupatiṣṭherannudvayantamasaspari jyotiḥ paśyanta uttaraṃ svaḥ paśyanta uttaraṃ devaṃ devatrā sūryyamaganma jyotiruttamamiti
2.12.d: आदित्यमुपतिष्ठेरन्नुद्वयन्तमसस्परि ज्योतिः पश्यन्त उत्तरं स्वः पश्यन्त उत्तरं देवं देवत्रा सूर्य्यमगन्म ज्योतिरुत्तममिति
2.12.m: They should attend upon the sun with: 'Arising from darkness, beholding the higher light, beholding the higher heaven, the god among the gods, we have attained the sun, the supreme light' (ud vayaṃ tamasas pari...).
If it has set, [they attend upon] the āhavanīya fire.

2.12.s: tasmin samidha ādadhyuredhosyedhiṣīmahīti prathamā samidasi samedhiṣīmahīti dvitīyāṃ yadenaścakṛmā vayaṃ yadvānyakṛtamārimānayā samidhā vay sarvantadapamṛjya ha iti tṛtīyām
2.12.d: तस्मिन् समिध आदध्युरेधोस्येधिषीमहीति प्रथमा समिदसि समेधिषीमहीति द्वितीयां यदेनश्चकृमा वयं यद्वान्यकृतमारिमानया समिधा वय् सर्वन्तदपमृज्य ह इति तृतीयाम्
2.12.m: They should put kindling sticks on it: the first with 'Thou art kindling, may we thrive' (edho 'sy edhiṣīmahi); the second with 'Thou art kindling, may we prosper' (samid asi samedhiṣīmahi); the third with 'Whatever sin we have committed, or what committed by another we have encountered, with this kindling stick may we wipe it all away' (yad enaś cakṛmā vayam...).

2.12.s: tamevopatiṣṭherannapo adyānvacāriṣaṃ rasena samaganmahi payasvānagna āgamantaṃ mā ssṛja varcaseti
2.12.d: तमेवोपतिष्ठेरन्नपो अद्यान्वचारिषं रसेन समगन्महि पयस्वानग्न आगमन्तं मा स्सृज वर्चसेति
2.12.m: They should attend upon that very fire with: 'We have entered the waters today, we have united with their essence; having come, rich in sap, O Agni, unite me with brilliance' (apo adyānvacāriṣam...).
Before the concluding atirātra sacrifice, the day ends with the apsuṣoma rites in sacrificial sessions.
In multi-day sacrifices, it ends with the consumption of curd.

2.12.s: yāvantyahāni rājānaṃ bhakṣayeyustāvatsvabrāhmaṇāyocchiṣṭaṃ na dadyuradbhirvā prokṣya dadyuḥ
