5.1.s: yajamānaṃ brūyātprabhūtamannaṃ kāraya suhitā alaṅkṛtā bhavatetyamātyān brūhi vatsāśca mātṛbhiḥ saha vāsayeta
5.1.d: यजमानं ब्रूयात्प्रभूतमन्नं कारय सुहिता अलङ्कृता भवतेत्यमात्यान् ब्रूहि वत्साश्च मातृभिः सह वासयेत
5.1.m: He should say to the patron of the sacrifice: 'Have plenty of food prepared; tell your attendants, "Be sated and adorned!"', and he should cause the calves to spend the night with their mothers.
In the forenoon, having seated the brahman priest, the adhvaryu priest offers the rice cooked with milk at the bellow of a bull.
If the bull does not bellow, the brahman priest himself should say, 'Offer!'
At the offering to the ancestors, he should do everything silently; he should assent with just 'Om'.

5.2.m: Regarding wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder or over the right shoulder, he should follow the adhvaryu priest.

5.2.s: tasyā havīṣi nirvapsyatsu dakṣiṇayā dvārā prapadya paścātprāṅmukha upaviśet
5.2.d: तस्या हवीषि निर्वप्स्यत्सु दक्षिणया द्वारा प्रपद्य पश्चात्प्राङ्मुख उपविशेत्
5.2.m: When they are about to apportion the oblations of that [sacrifice], having entered through the southern door, he should sit down in the west facing east.
Just so, having gone to the altar when they are about to take away the ritual grass-clump.
When the two portions of clarified butter have been offered, having gone south of the fire, he and the patron of the sacrifice should sit down in the east facing west.
When the Sviṣṭakṛt offering has been made, having returned the way they came, they should sit down.
Having smelled the prāśitra portion that has been brought, he should cast it away.
If they cut off clarified butter from the prāśitra portion, having smelled that, he should touch water.
And having received the iḍā portion, he should return it.

5.2.s: akṣannamīmadanta hīti prathamā susaṃdṛśaṃ tvā vayaṃ maghavanmandiṣīmahi pranūnaṃ pūrṇavandhuraḥ sruto yāsi vaśāanu yojā nvindra te harī iti dvitīyopo ṣu śṛṇuhī gira iti tṛtīyā
5.2.d: अक्षन्नमीमदन्त हीति प्रथमा सुसंदृशं त्वा वयं मघवन्मन्दिषीमहि प्रनूनं पूर्णवन्धुरः स्रुतो यासि वशाअनु योजा न्विन्द्र ते हरी इति द्वितीयोपो षु शृणुही गिर इति तृतीया
5.2.m: 'They have eaten, they have rejoiced…' is the first [verse]; 'May we delight in you, O generous one, of fair appearance; now indeed, with full chariot-seat, you go along flowing streams according to your wish; yoke now, O Indra, your two bay steeds' is the second; 'Hearken well to our songs' is the third.

5.2.s: tata evekṣamāṇā gārhapatyaṃ manonvāhuvāmahe nārāśsena somena pitṝṇāñca manmabhiḥ punarnaḥ pitaro mano dadātu daivo jano jīvaṃ brātsace mahyā na etu manaḥ punaḥ kratve dakṣāya jīvase jyokca sūryaṃ dṛśe yamiti
5.2.d: तत एवेक्षमाणा गार्हपत्यं मनोन्वाहुवामहे नाराश्सेन सोमेन पितॄणाञ्च मन्मभिः पुनर्नः पितरो मनो ददातु दैवो जनो जीवं ब्रात्सचे मह्या न एतु मनः पुनः क्रत्वे दक्षाय जीवसे ज्योक्च सूर्यं दृशे यमिति
5.2.m: Looking from that very place at the gārhapatya fire, [with the verses]: 'We summon the mind back with the Nārāśaṃsa soma and with the thoughts of the ancestors; may our ancestors give us back our mind; may the divine folk [join] the living folk; may we unite; may our mind come back to us for resolve, for skill, for life, and long to see the sun.'
[And they attend upon] the southern fire with the single [verse]: 'With what wonderful aid will he be present for us…'

5.3.m: The cakes called Traiyambaka are baked on a single potsherd.

5.3.s: teṣāṃ yamadhvaryurākhatkara upopet tatrāpaṃ upaspṛśeyuḥ śivā naḥ śanta mā bhava sumṛḍīkā sarasvati mā te vyoma sandaśa iti
5.3.d: तेषां यमध्वर्युराखत्कर उपोपेत् तत्रापं उपस्पृशेयुः शिवा नः शन्त मा भव सुमृडीका सरस्वति मा ते व्योम सन्दश इति
5.3.m: Of those, whatever the adhvaryu priest approaches on the molehill, there they should touch water with: 'Be propitious, most benevolent to us, very gracious, O Sarasvatī; may we not see any emptiness in you.'
Dhānañjayya says: He should remain seated while the others are being offered.

5.3.s: hute tiṣṭhanto japeyuravāmba rudramayakṣmahyavadevaṃ tryambaka yathā naḥ śreyasaskaradyathā no vasīyasaskaradyathā naḥ paśumataskaradyathā nau vyavasāyayādbheṣajamasi bheṣajaṅgave'śvāya puruṣāya bheṣajsugaṃ meṣāya meṣyaisu bheṣajaṃ yathā saditi
5.3.d: हुते तिष्ठन्तो जपेयुरवाम्ब रुद्रमयक्ष्मह्यवदेवं त्र्यम्बक यथा नः श्रेयसस्करद्यथा नो वसीयसस्करद्यथा नः पशुमतस्करद्यथा नौ व्यवसाययाद्भेषजमसि भेषजङ्गवेऽश्वाय पुरुषाय भेषज्सुगं मेषाय मेष्यैसु भेषजं यथा सदिति
5.3.m: When it has been offered, standing, they should mutter: 'We have appeased Rudra, mother! We have appeased the god Tryambaka, so that he may make us better off, so that he may make us wealthier, so that he may make us possessors of cattle, so that he may grant us perseverance. You are medicine, medicine for cow, horse, and man; medicine for ram and ewe, so that there may be medicine!'
The attendants of the patron of the sacrifice, taking one cake each, should walk three times sunwise around the fire.

5.3.s: tatra brahmā pariyañjapediti dhānañjayyastiṣṭhanniti śāṇḍilyastryambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ puṣṭivarddhanamurvārukamiva bandhanān mṛtyormukṣīyamāmṛtāditi
5.3.d: तत्र ब्रह्मा परियञ्जपेदिति धानञ्जय्यस्तिष्ठन्निति शाण्डिल्यस्त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्द्धनमुर्वारुकमिव बन्धनान् मृत्योर्मुक्षीयमामृतादिति
5.3.m: There Dhānañjayya says that the brahman priest should mutter while walking around; Śāṇḍilya says while standing: 'We sacrifice to Tryambaka, the sweet-scented increaser of prosperity; as a cucumber from its stem, may I be freed from death, not from immortality.'

5.3.s: teṣāṃ brahmaikaṃ lipsitvā yasya sa syāttasmai prayacchet
5.3.d: तेषां ब्रह्मैकं लिप्सित्वा यस्य स स्यात्तस्मै प्रयच्छेत्
5.3.m: Having desired to obtain one of them, the brahman priest should hand it to him whose it is.
Or else he should touch it while it remains in his hand.
In the same manner, they should walk around in reverse.

5.3.d: यत्रैनानध्वर्युरासजेत्तत्रोपतिष्ठेरन्नेष ते रुद्र भागस्तेनावसेन परोमूजवतीतीहि कृत्तिवासाः पिनाकहस्तोऽवततधन्वोमित्यातमितोरुपेयुः
5.3.m: Wherever the adhvaryu priest fastens them, there they should attend upon them with: 'This is your share, O Rudra; with this provision go beyond the Mūjavant mountains, clad in animal skin, Pināka in hand, with unstrung bow! Om'—chanting until they are exhausted.
Having touched water with: 'May the divine [waters] be propitious to us…', they should return without looking back.
The duty of the brahman priest in the haviryajña offerings is explained by the Varuṇapraghāsa rites.
When they are about to offer the libation on the sacrificial post for the animal victims, he should sit down silently.

5.3.s: vapāyā hutāyāmidamāpa iti cātvāle mārjayitvā sarvapaśūnāṃ yathārthsyāt
5.3.d: वपाया हुतायामिदमाप इति चात्वाले मार्जयित्वा सर्वपशूनां यथार्थ्स्यात्
5.3.m: When the omentum has been offered, having performed ablutions at the cātvāla pit with: 'Here, O waters…', for all the animal victims he may act according to need.

5.4.s: āhṛtaṃ puroḍāśamālabhya brūyāt prāśnantu ye prāśiṣyanta iti
5.4.d: आहृतं पुरोडाशमालभ्य ब्रूयात् प्राश्नन्तु ये प्राशिष्यन्त इति
5.4.m: Having touched the sacrificial cake that has been brought, he should say: 'Let those who are to eat, eat!'
Dhānañjayya says: He should follow along with the offerings to the wives of the gods for all the animal victims.
Gautama says: Only for the animal victim belonging to the soma pressing.
Śāṇḍilya says: Neither for that nor for the victim belonging to the soma pressing.

5.4.s: hṛdayaśūlo'trāvabhṛthanyaṅgasthāne bhavati tasminnapa upaspṛśeyurddhāmno dhāmno rājstato varuṇa no muñca yadāpo aghnyā varuṇeti śapāmahe tato varuṇa nomuñca sumitriyā na āpa oṣadhayaḥ santu durmitriyāstasmai santu yo'smān dveṣṭi yañca vayandviṣma iti
5.4.d: हृदयशूलोऽत्रावभृथन्यङ्गस्थाने भवति तस्मिन्नप उपस्पृशेयुर्द्धाम्नो धाम्नो राज्स्ततो वरुण नो मुञ्च यदापो अघ्न्या वरुणेति शपामहे ततो वरुण नोमुञ्च सुमित्रिया न आप ओषधयः सन्तु दुर्मित्रियास्तस्मै सन्तु योऽस्मान् द्वेष्टि यञ्च वयन्द्विष्म इति
5.4.m: Here the spit used for roasting the heart takes the place of the concluding purificatory bath part; upon it they should touch water with: 'From abode to abode, O King, from there release us, O Varuṇa! If we swear by the inviolable waters, O Varuṇa, release us from that, O Varuṇa! Friendly to us may the waters and plants be; unfriendly may they be to him who hates us and whom we hate!'
From here onwards it proceeds beginning with the sprinkling of water.
They should not attend upon the sun.
Having sat while the full oblation is being offered, when it has been offered, he may act according to need.
If they offer the offerings of barley meal, he should sit until their offering.
In the Sautrāmaṇī, he should sit while approaching the rites concerning the liquor.
There he carries forward two fires beyond.

5.4.s: dakṣiṇamadhyadhikumbhyāmāsaktāyā surāśeṣeṣvāsicyamāneṣūpatiṣṭheranyatte pavitramarcciṣyagne vitatamantaraṃ brahma tena punīhi meti
5.4.d: दक्षिणमध्यधिकुम्भ्यामासक्ताया सुराशेषेष्वासिच्यमानेषूपतिष्ठेरन्यत्ते पवित्रमर्च्चिष्यग्ने विततमन्तरं ब्रह्म तेन पुनीहि मेति
5.4.m: When the southern [vessel] is attached over the two jars and the liquor residues are being poured in, they should attend with: 'Whatever purifying filter is spread out within the flame, O Agni, with that brahman purify me!'

5.4.s: aśvinorgrahasya bhakṣayedyamaśvinā namucerāsurādadhi sarasvatyasunodindriyeṇemant śukraṃ madhumantamindsomrājānamiha bhakṣayāmīti bhakṣayet
5.4.d: अश्विनोर्ग्रहस्य भक्षयेद्यमश्विना नमुचेरासुरादधि सरस्वत्यसुनोदिन्द्रियेणेमन्त् शुक्रं मधुमन्तमिन्द्सोम्राजानमिह भक्षयामीति भक्षयेत्
5.4.m: He should consume from the cup of the Aśvins; he should consume it with: 'What the Aśvins and Sarasvatī pressed out from the asura Namuci with power—this bright, honeyed soma, King Indra, here I consume.'

5.4.s: yajamānañcedvasātiśeṣeṇābhiṣiñceyurupotthāyāntareṇāgnī gatvādhvaryuṇoktaḥ sśānāni gāyet padāya padāya stobhet
5.4.d: यजमानञ्चेद्वसातिशेषेणाभिषिञ्चेयुरुपोत्थायान्तरेणाग्नी गत्वाध्वर्युणोक्तः स्शानानि गायेत् पदाय पदाय स्तोभेत्
5.4.m: If they consecrate the patron of the sacrifice with the remainder of the vasātīvari water, having risen up and gone between the two fires, being addressed by the adhvaryu priest, he should sing the sāmans and make stobha interjections pada by pada.
Reaching the cadences, they should touch the head of the patron of the sacrifice.
With the verses beginning 'Let them be…' and 'They urge…', the preceding stoma comes first, and the following is the cadence.

5.4.s: śravasaḥ sthāne sañjityai vijityai satyajityai jityā iti kṣattriyasya sampuṣṭyai vipuṣṭyai satyapuṣṭyai puṣṭyā iti vaiśyasya
5.4.d: श्रवसः स्थाने सञ्जित्यै विजित्यै सत्यजित्यै जित्या इति क्षत्त्रियस्य सम्पुष्ट्यै विपुष्ट्यै सत्यपुष्ट्यै पुष्ट्या इति वैश्यस्य
5.4.m: In place of the word śravas, 'for complete victory, for triumph, for true conquest, for victory' for a kṣatriya; 'for complete abundance, for thriving, for true prosperity, for nourishment' for a vaiśya.
There are two Sautrāmaṇī rites: the Kaukilī and the Carakasautrāmaṇī.
In the Kaukilī there is the singing of sāmans, not in the other.
There are seven forms of haviryajña and seven forms of somayajña.

5.4.s: tāsāhaviryajñassthānāmagnyādheyamagnihotraṃ darśapūrṇamāsau cāturmāsyāni paśubandhaḥ sautrāmaṇī pākayajña iti
5.4.d: तासाहविर्यज्ञस्स्थानामग्न्याधेयमग्निहोत्रं दर्शपूर्णमासौ चातुर्मास्यानि पशुबन्धः सौत्रामणी पाकयज्ञ इति
5.4.m: Among those forms of haviryajña are: the establishment of the sacred fires, the Agnihotra, the new- and full-moon sacrifices, the four-monthly sacrifices, the animal sacrifice, the Sautrāmaṇī, and the domestic cooking sacrifice.

5.4.s: atha somassthā agniṣṭomo'tyagniṣṭoma ukthyaḥ ṣoḍaśyatirātro vājapeyo'ptoryāma ityaptoryāma iti
5.4.d: अथ सोमस्स्था अग्निष्टोमोऽत्यग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यः षोडश्यतिरात्रो वाजपेयोऽप्तोर्याम इत्यप्तोर्याम इति
5.4.m: Now the soma-sacrifice forms: agniṣṭoma, atyagniṣṭoma, ukthya, ṣoḍaśin, atirātra, vājapeya, aptoryāma—thus the aptoryāma.
